Fleet Manager never talks to the flight controller directly. UAVcast-Pro on the drone's companion computer does that, and keeps one encrypted connection to Fleet Manager: Pairing. UAVcast-Pro asks Fleet Manager for a pairing code. You type the code into Fleet Manager. Fleet Manager then hands the drone its own client certificate. Control channel. The drone connects to Fleet Manager's MQTT broker over TLS on port 8883, authenticated with that certificate. Telemetry, heartbeats, commands, terminal sessions and remote access to the UAVcast-Pro web interface all travel over this connection. It works through NAT and cellular networks because the drone always connects outward. Data channel (optional). Video and MAVLink to a ground station go peer to peer over your organization's private VPN, a WireGuard network run by Fleet Manager. Without VPN, Fleet Manager still shows and controls the drone, but it doesn't route streams.

t: What do I need to use Fleet Manager?
c: A UAVmatrix account, and drones running UAVcast-Pro with an activated license. Each drone's license must be owned by a member of your organization. See Licenses and seats.
No. Fleet Manager is included with your UAVcast-Pro license. There is no separate subscription, and team members are free.

t: How many drones can I manage?
c: Fleet Manager itself sets no limit. Each drone needs its own UAVcast-Pro license activation, so the number of drones follows the licenses and device slots you own.

t: Do team members need a license?
c: No. Invite as many Admins and Viewers as you need. See Invite your team.
Owner, Admin and Viewer. There is no "Member" role. See Roles and permissions.

t: Where does the pairing code come from?
c: From the drone. In UAVcast-Pro, open Fleet Management → Connect to Fleet Manager. It shows an 8-digit code that is valid for 5 minutes. You type it into Fleet Manager under Fleet → Pair Device. See Add your first drone.
Yes. The drone connects outward to Fleet Manager on TCP 8883, so it works behind carrier NAT without a public IP. The carrier must not block port 8883.

Only to send video and telemetry from drones to ground stations through Fleet Manager. The map, telemetry, commands, missions, terminal and remote access to UAVcast-Pro all work without it. See Network and VPN.

t: Can one ground station receive several drones?
c: Yes. Each stream binding gets its own block of ports on that ground station, with room for a second camera and audio. The first drone uses 5600 / 14550.

t: Can I keep using my own ZeroTier or Tailscale network?
c: Yes, if you don't need Fleet Manager's stream bindings. You can decline VPN when pairing. If you accept, a drone already on a Tailscale network is moved to your organization's network. A drone on ZeroTier keeps its ZeroTier network and joins the organization's network alongside it; ZeroTier is only left when you unpair the drone.

t: Does it work with ArduPilot and PX4?
c: Fleet Manager works with any MAVLink flight controller that UAVcast-Pro talks to, ArduPilot or PX4: live map, telemetry, status, the terminal and stream bindings are the same. The flight-mode controls use ArduPilot's modes for Copter, Plane, Rover and Sub, and the mission command list follows ArduPilot naming, so on PX4 change modes and plan missions from your ground station.

t: Can I fly a drone from Fleet Manager alone?
c: Fleet Manager can change modes, arm, and start, pause and stop missions. It is not built for manual stick control. Always keep a pilot with a ground station or RC transmitter in control, and follow your local regulations.

t: How long is flight history kept?
c: Up to 1 year by default. Owners and Admins can shorten it to 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days or 6 months. See Flight history.
Not today. Fleet Manager replays flights on the map but doesn't export files or store .tlog, DataFlash or video.

t: Does Fleet Manager send alerts by email?
c: Not yet. Status is shown live on the map, fleet list and UAV pages. See Status indicators and notifications.

t: What happens when a drone loses its connection?
c: After 20 seconds without data it is shown as OFFLINE, and it reconnects by itself when its link comes back. The flight controller's own failsafes decide what the aircraft does; Fleet Manager doesn't command anything on connection loss.

t: How do I move a drone to another organization?
c: Remove it from the current organization (this deletes its history there), then pair it into the new one. See Remove or transfer a drone.

t: I bought licenses with a different email. What now?
c: Invite that email to the organization, or ask support to add it as an extra license email on your account. See Licenses bought with another email.

p: Re-pair, remove or transfer a drone
b: Fleet Manager › Fleet & UAVs › Re-pair, remove or transfer a drone
c: Fleet Manager has no "transfer" button for a single drone, because history stays with the organization that recorded it. To move a drone: In the current organization, remove the drone. Its history there is deleted. Make sure the drone's UAVcast-Pro license is owned by a member of the new organization. See Licenses. In the new organization, pair the drone. p: Re-pair, remove or transfer a drone
b: Fleet Manager › Fleet & UAVs › Re-pair, remove or transfer a drone
c: Fleet Manager identifies a drone by a device ID that UAVcast-Pro computes from the companion computer's CPU serial number and its boot disk (SD card or SSD). A new companion computer, or a new SD card or SSD in the same one, shows up as a new drone. Reinstalling UAVcast-Pro on the same board and disk keeps the same device ID. Remove the old drone in Fleet Manager (or keep it until you no longer need its history). Install UAVcast-Pro on the new computer and activate the license. See Activate your license. Pair it as a new drone and recreate its stream bindings.

A drone's page in Fleet Manager shows live telemetry and companion computer health, an SSH terminal and MAVLink log, and reboot or remove. Each drone has its own page. Open it with Details on the Fleet card, from the dashboard, or with View UAV at the end of pairing. The header shows the name, a live status badge, Re-pair required if needed, the organization, the device ID and Last seen. Owners and Admins also get Rename and Remove. The page has four tabs: Overview, Terminal, Logs and Actions.

b: Fleet Manager › Fleet & UAVs › UAV details
c: Live data, pushed to the browser as it arrives. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/drone-detail Overview tab of an armed VTOL in AUTO: UAVcast Application card with CPU Temp, CPU, Memory and Disk, and the MAVLink / Flight Controller card with battery, GPS, altitude and heading. UAVcast Application describes the companion computer: connection state (Connected, Waiting for data... or Connecting...), Hostname, Uptime, CPU Temp, CPU, Memory and Disk usage, the UAVcast-Pro services and their state, and the drone's network addresses (LAN and VPN). It also has the buttons to open UAVcast-Pro remotely: Open via Proxy and, when the drone is on the VPN, Open via VPN. MAVLink / Flight Controller shows what the flight controller reports: ARMED or DISARMED, FAILSAFE and GCS FAILSAFE flags, Battery, GPS (satellites and fix), Altitude and Heading. Watch CPU Temp on hot days A Raspberry Pi that runs hot slows down, and video is the first thing to suffer. If CPU Temp climbs during a flight, see Undervoltage and throttling.

b: Fleet Manager › Fleet & UAVs › UAV details
c: Below the cards, Connected Ground Stations lists the ground stations that receive this drone's streams, with Video and Telemetry switches and Pause / Resume. Add GCS (Owners and Admins) binds another ground station to this drone. It creates the same stream binding as Network → Stream Bindings, with the next free ports on that ground station, and sends the new destination to the drone. See Stream bindings.

b: Fleet Manager › Fleet & UAVs › UAV details
c: A browser SSH session to the companion computer, over Fleet Manager's encrypted connection. No port forwarding and no VPN needed. Owners and Admins only. The drone must be online. Select Connect to open a shell. Quick-command buttons run common checks for you: df -h, free -h, top -bn1, ip a, ip r, uptime, dmesg and ps aux. Disconnect closes the session. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/drone-detail Terminal tab connected to a field drone, after running the df -h quick command. This is a live shell on the aircraft The terminal is a real shell on the companion computer. Restarting services or the network while the drone is in the air can cut telemetry and video. Use it on the ground unless you know what a command does.

b: Fleet Manager › Fleet & UAVs › UAV details
c: A live view of the telemetry and heartbeat messages the drone sends to Fleet Manager, with Telemetry and Heartbeat filters, Auto-scroll, Pause and clear. Download logs saves what is on screen to a text file (mavlink-log-<id>-<time>.txt), which is useful to email to support with your ticket number (tickets only take an image). This is a live log, not a flight log archive. Fleet Manager stores telemetry for flight history, but doesn't store or export DataFlash or .tlog files. Those stay on the flight controller and in your ground station software. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/drone-detail Logs tab streaming TELEMETRY and HEARTBEAT entries, with Telemetry, Heartbeat and Auto-scroll on.

b: Fleet Manager › Fleet & UAVs › UAV details
c: System Actions has Reboot (Restart the companion computer) and Shutdown (Power off the companion computer). Both need the drone to be online. To confirm, you type the action's name. How UAVcast-Pro licenses and device slots decide which drones you can pair in Fleet Manager, and how to use licenses bought with another email. Fleet Manager is included with your UAVcast-Pro license. It doesn't have its own subscription, seats or plans. What you can pair is decided by your UAVcast-Pro licenses from the UAVmatrix store: Drones: every paired drone runs UAVcast-Pro with an activated license. Each activation uses one of the license's Device Slots in the store ("2 of 5 device slots used"). Need more drones? Buy more licenses or slots. Fleet → Need more devices? → View Plans takes you to the store. Team members: free. Fleet Manager doesn't limit how many people you invite, and members don't need a license of their own. Fleet Manager is included with a UAVcast-Pro license. Each drone you pair needs one. Buy UAVcast-ProSee plans and pricing

t: What Fleet Manager checks when you pair
c: When you enter a pairing code, Fleet Manager looks up the license that is activated on that drone and checks that: the license exists and is active, not expired and not refunded, and its owner's email (the store account that bought it) belongs to a member of the organization you are pairing into, in any role. If both are true, the drone is paired. Fleet Manager checks again whenever the drone is re-paired. Message in the pairing wizardMeaning License is not owned by any member of this organization The license belongs to a store account whose email isn't a member here. License has expired The license's expiry date has passed. License has been refunded The license was returned. Invalid license key The store doesn't know the license on the drone. Check the activation in UAVcast-Pro. The license is also checked one step earlier, when UAVcast-Pro asks for a pairing code. If UAVcast-Pro shows Invalid or inactive license instead of a code, the license is expired, refunded or not linked to a store account. For activation problems on the drone itself, see Activate your license and License won't activate.

Fleet Manager matches by email, so plan who buys: Simplest: the organization's Owner buys all licenses with the email they sign in to Fleet Manager with. Several buyers: any member's licenses count, Viewers included. A purchasing colleague can be a Viewer. Customer-owned drones: if a customer bought the licenses, invite the customer's store email to your organization (Viewer is enough).

A common case: licenses were bought with purchasing@company.com, but the pilot signs in to Fleet Manager as anna@company.com. Pairing fails with License is not owned by any member of this organization. You have two ways to fix it: Invite the buying email to the organization. That account must sign in once to accept the invitation. Ask UAVmatrix support to add a license email to your account. Support can add one or more extra emails to a Fleet Manager user. Licenses owned by any of those emails then count as that user's when pairing, in every organization the user belongs to. To request it, open a ticket from the support bubble (category General Inquiry) or email support@uavmatrix.com from the address you sign in with, and list the other email(s) the licenses were bought with. See Support. Good to know: Emails are matched without regard to upper or lower case. Each extra email can belong to one Fleet Manager user only. Only UAVmatrix support can add or remove these emails. They don't appear in your own settings. The licenses stay in the original store account. This only changes who Fleet Manager counts as the owner when you pair.

A license is activated per device in UAVcast-Pro, not in Fleet Manager. To move one, free the device slot in UAVcast-Pro or the store, activate it on the new drone, then pair the new drone. See Replace the companion computer.

Lite view is Fleet Manager's phone-sized control screen: fleet list, live battery, GPS and altitude, flight modes and mission start, pause and RTL. Lite Control is a phone-friendly version of Fleet Manager for use in the field: big buttons, the essentials only, and live updates over your phone's mobile data.

c: On your phone, sign in to Fleet Manager, open the menu and select Fleet → Lite View. You can also go straight to https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/lite. Add it to your home screen for one-tap access.

The list shows every drone with its status and battery (orange below 40 %, red below 20 %), a Live updates active indicator and the count n online / n total. Tap a drone to open its control screen. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/lite Lite view on a 390 × 844 phone: Fleet list with 33 online / 46 total, flight mode and battery per drone.

Banners for Vehicle Armed and Failsafe Active. Cards for Battery, GPS, Altitude and Speed. Device ID, Organization, Position and View Full Details (opens the full UAV page). fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/lite Lite view for an armed drone in AUTO: Vehicle Armed banner, Battery, GPS, Altitude and Speed cards, and the mode and mission controls.

Lite view shows ARMED (Motors active - exercise caution) or DISARMED (Safe to approach), but has no arm or disarm button: For safety, arm/disarm should be performed via your Ground Control Station (QGC, Mission Planner).

Quick Access shows the modes you use most for the vehicle type, All Modes the full list. Safe modes switch after a simple confirmation; navigation and dangerous modes ask Change to MODE? with a stronger check, as in the control panel.

For a mission already on the drone: Start / Resume, Pause, RTL and Stop, each with a confirmation. Rovers use HOLD instead of LOITER to pause and stop. Jump to Waypoint: pick the number with − and +, then Jump to WP n. Currently at waypoint n shows progress. Refresh Mission Data reloads the mission from the drone. If the drone has no mission, you see No Mission Loaded. Upload one from Missions on a computer first.

Track every drone in your fleet on one live map with status rings, heading lines, 5-minute trails, follow mode and OpenAIP airspace layers. Fleet Map (sidebar Overview → Fleet Map) shows every drone in the selected organization on one map, updated live as telemetry arrives. It is built for a control room: leave it open and you see at a glance which aircraft are up, where they are heading and which ones need attention. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/map Fleet Map on the Dark style over the Port of Rotterdam: each drone in its own color with heading line and trail, and grey offline markers labelled with how long ago they were seen.

c: Each drone is drawn in its own color, with an icon for its vehicle type: quadcopter, hexacopter, plane, VTOL, rover, boat or submarine. Rings and badges around the marker flag problems: On the markerMeaning Drone's own color, no ring Online and healthy. Grey marker, grey dashed ring and clock badge Offline: nothing received for 20 seconds. Orange ring with ! badge NO MAVLINK: UAVcast-Pro is online but has had no telemetry from the flight controller for 10 seconds. Check the flight controller connection. Red dashed ring GPS lost: no satellites or no fix. Yellow dashed ring GPS weak: fewer than 6 satellites or only a 2D fix. H marker The drone's home position, set when it arms. Hover to see its altitude (AMSL). Armed or disarmed isn't shown by the marker itself. Open the popup, or use the control panel, to see Armed. The label next to the marker reads Name • FLIGHTMODE, with NO MAVLINK, NO GPS or WEAK GPS added when they apply, or Name • OFFLINE • 5 mins ago for an offline drone.

The heading line is a dashed line in the drone's color pointing where the nose points. It is hidden when the drone is offline. The flight trail shows the last 5 minutes of the path, as a dashed line in the drone's color (grey when offline). A new point is added about every 11 m of movement.

Select a marker to open its popup: name, organization and status, then Battery, Altitude, Mode, Armed, GPS (satellites and fix type: No Fix, 2D, 3D, DGPS or RTK), Signal and, when offline, Last seen. The latest status message from the flight controller appears too, which is often the fastest way to read a pre-arm failure. Signal is the round-trip time between Fleet Manager and the drone, measured every 10 seconds: excellent under 100 ms, good under 300 ms, fair under 600 ms, poor above that or after three missed pings. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/map Popup for an armed survey drone in AUTO: Battery 71%, Altitude 85.5 m, GPS 20 sats (3D), Signal 61 ms (Excellent), with Follow, History and Controls. Three buttons: Follow keeps the drone in view. See below. History opens flight history for this drone. Controls opens the UAV Control Panel.

Select Follow in the popup. The map zooms in (to at least zoom level 14) and centers on the drone, then pans only when the drone gets close to the edge of the screen, so the map doesn't jitter. A Following name banner appears; select its X, or Unfollow, to stop. Opening History also stops following. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/map Follow mode on a fixed-wing mapping a corridor, with the Following banner and the trail behind it.
Drones that are online but have no position yet are listed in a drones without GPS box on the map. Select one to open its control panel. The counter n drones on map tells you how many are plotted.

Select the gear button at the top right to open Map Settings. Your choices are saved in this browser. SectionOptionDefault Overlays Airspace Layers: restricted airspace, airports, heliports Off Drone Filter All Drones, Online Only or Offline Only All Drones Marker Options Heading Line On Marker Tooltip: name label on markers On Always Visible: show the label permanently instead of on hover On Flight Trail: recent flight path (last 5 min) On Map Style Satellite, Light or Dark Dark fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/map Map Settings panel with Airspace Layers on, Drone Filter set to Online Only and Map Style Satellite. For a busy map With 20+ drones in one area, switch Always Visible off so labels only appear on hover, and use Online Only to hide parked aircraft.

Airspace Layers draws restricted airspace, airports and heliports from OpenAIP on top of the map. The layer appears from zoom level 7 and closer. It is one combined layer; you can't toggle categories separately. Not a substitute for official airspace checks The airspace layer is for situational awareness. Check NOTAMs and your national drone map or UTM service before each flight.

Replay a drone's recorded flight on the Fleet Manager map, read duration, max altitude and speed, save named flights and set telemetry retention. Fleet Manager records each drone's telemetry once per second while it is connected: position, altitude, speed, heading, battery, flight mode, armed state and GPS. Flight history replays that recording on the map.

The drawer name - Flight History opens at the bottom of the map. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/map Flight history for an inspection drone: the saved flight Turbine blade inspection selected, playback at 4x, and Duration, Max Alt, Max Speed and Avg Battery.

b: Fleet Manager › Live map › Flight history
c: Select flight session lists: Saved flights first (with a bookmark icon), the ones your team has named. Then one entry per day with recorded telemetry, for the last 30 days. A day groups all telemetry from that date, so several flights on one day appear as one session. Save the stretch you care about as a named flight to find it again quickly.

b: Fleet Manager › Live map › Flight history
c: Play and pause, step back or forward by 5 % of the session, or jump to the start or end. Drag the timeline to scrub. Speeds: 0.5x, 1x (real time), 2x, 4x, 8x, 10x and 20x. Keyboard: Space play/pause, ← / → step, Esc close. On the map, a green Start and a red End marker frame the flight. The part already played is drawn in cyan, the rest dashed in grey, and a drone icon labelled with its altitude moves along the path. The stats panel shows Duration, Max Alt, Max Speed and Avg Battery, and Current Position shows Alt, Speed, Heading and Mode at the playback point.

b: Fleet Manager › Live map › Flight history
c: Owners and Admins can save, rename and delete named flights. Viewers can play them back. Save and name this flight saves the current time range under a name (up to 100 characters), for example "Survey over Field A". Two saved flights can't overlap: A saved session already exists for this time range. Rename flight changes the name. Delete saved flight removes the name only. Delete Saved Flight? explains that the telemetry itself is not deleted.

b: Fleet Manager › Live map › Flight history
c: Owners and Admins set retention per organization in Settings → History (Telemetry History): Retention: 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days, 6 months or 1 year. The default and the maximum is 1 year. Prune Now deletes data older than 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days right away (default 30), after the Prune Old History confirmation. Delete Drone History (trash icon per drone) or Select All → Delete Selected (n) clears history for chosen drones. Cards show Storage Used, Total Records and Retention. Fleet Manager removes data past the retention period once a day. Older data is compressed after 7 days, so a year of history for a large fleet stays practical. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/settings Settings → History for an organization with 46 drones: Storage Used, Total Records, Retention 90 days, and the per-drone list with Delete buttons. No log export Fleet Manager doesn't export flight history as a file, and it doesn't store video or flight controller logs (.tlog, DataFlash). Keep those from your ground station software or the flight controller's SD card. For video recordings on the drone, see Recordings and flight review. Removing a drone deletes its whole history, saved flights included. See Remove or transfer a drone.

c: Select Create New (or Missions → New Mission). Click on the map to add waypoints. Drag a waypoint to move it. While placing, Next WP shows the distance from the previous waypoint (Prev:) and from home (Home:). Open the waypoint drawer (n Waypoints) to edit each row: Command, Params, Alt, Frame and Radius. Drag rows to reorder. Row H is home. Set Defaults: for new waypoints at the top of the drawer: Alt (default 50 m) and WP Radius (default 30 m). fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/missions Waypoint drawer with a Takeoff, several Waypoint rows, a Change Speed and a Return to Launch, Frame set to Relative.
FrameAltitude is measured from Relative (default) The home position Absolute Mean sea level Terrain The ground below the waypoint (needs terrain data on the flight controller)

The Command picker is searchable and lists the MAVLink mission commands ArduPilot understands, grouped as: Navigation: Waypoint, Takeoff, Land, Return to Launch, Loiter Unlim, Loiter Turns, Loiter Time, Loiter to Alt, Spline Waypoint, Vtol Takeoff, Vtol Land, Payload Place, Delay and more. Conditions: Delay, Change Alt, Distance, Yaw. Do commands: Change Speed, Set ROI Location, Set Servo, Set Relay, Jump, Digicam Control, Set Cam Trigg Dist, Mount Control, Gripper, Parachute, VTOL Transition and others. Commands that take parameters (for example delay time, loiter turns, speed or servo PWM) get editable fields in Params. Limits: altitude 0 to 10,000 m, radius 1 to 1,000 m, at least one waypoint.

Select Save, enter a Name (up to 100 characters) and an optional Description, and confirm Save Mission. The header shows Unsaved while there are changes; Update Mission saves them. Open saved missions from Missions → Saved Missions.

Save the mission. An unsaved mission can't be uploaded (Mission not saved). Select Upload to Drone, choose the UAV under Select UAV and confirm. Wait for the confirmation. The upload times out after 30 seconds if the drone doesn't answer. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/missions Upload Mission to Drone dialog with the online UAVs to choose from. To fly it, select the mission in the drone's control panel and select Start. If the mission on the drone differs from the one you selected, the panel offers Upload & Start.

t: Read a mission from a drone
c: Under Missions → Read from Drone, choose an online drone. Its current mission loads into the planner as Mission from name. Save it to keep a copy, for example before you overwrite it. Check the mission in your ground station before flight Fleet Manager uploads exactly what you planned. Before an automatic flight, check the mission and the vehicle's failsafes in QGroundControl or Mission Planner, as you would with any other planning tool.

Enable your organization's private WireGuard VPN in Fleet Manager, connect drones and ground station laptops, and manage the devices table. Every organization can have its own private VPN: a WireGuard mesh network between your drones and your ground stations, run by Fleet Manager. On it, each device gets a fixed 100.x.y.z address and can reach the others directly, whether it is on 4G, Wi-Fi or satellite, without port forwarding or public IP addresses. Fleet Manager uses this network to route stream bindings: video and MAVLink from a drone to the laptops where pilots run QGroundControl or Mission Planner. All of this is on Network (sidebar Fleet Management → Network).
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

c: VPN is optional: Fleet Manager shows, maps and controls drones without it, over the drone's own encrypted connection. Turn it on when you want streams to reach ground stations. VPN recommendedVPN not required Drone and ground station on different networks (4G, remote sites) Drone and ground station on the same local Wi-Fi You want direct video and telemetry streaming You use a direct USB or serial telemetry link You need encrypted links between sites You are testing in a controlled environment You operate across several locations

Owners and Admins only. Open Network. If VPN is off, the page shows Enable VPN Network with what it gives you: secure WireGuard-based connections, low-latency video and telemetry streaming, and working across any network. Select Enable VPN Network. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/network Network page before VPN is enabled, with the three benefits and the Enable VPN Network button. Once VPN is on, the page shows four counters (Total Devices, Online, UAVs, Ground Stations) and three tabs: Devices, Stream Bindings and Settings. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/network Network → Devices for a large operator: Total Devices 51, Online 39, UAVs 44, Ground Stations 7, and the Connected Devices table.

Drones never need a manual command. There are two ways: When pairing. If VPN is enabled before you pair, the wizard's VPN Connection step joins the drone. See Add your first drone. Push to Drone. For drones paired before VPN was enabled, the Push to Drone card on the Devices tab lists every drone that isn't on your network. Select Connect next to a drone to send it the VPN settings. The drone must be online. If a drone is already on another Tailscale network, it has an Existing VPN badge. Connect then asks for confirmation (Existing VPN Connection Detected) and Replace & Connect moves it to your organization's network. The drone appears in Connected Devices with the UAV type and its VPN address, and the UAV page gets an Open via VPN button.

t: Put ground stations on the VPN
c: Ground stations join with one Tailscale command from Connect a Device. Follow Connect a ground station.

The table lists every device on the network: ColumnShows Status Online or offline on the VPN Device Name and hostname Type UAV, GCS or Unknown. Unknown devices have a Configure button. IP Address The device's VPN address (100.x.y.z) Last Check-in When the device was last seen on the network Select Sync to refresh the list from the VPN server. Each row's actions menu has: Rename: a readable name, for example "Field laptop – Team North". Change Type: switch between UAV, GCS and Unknown. For a UAV, choose which paired drone it is. Remove Device: takes the device off the network. For a drone, Fleet Manager tells it to leave the VPN, and its stream bindings are removed.

New ground stations show up as Unknown, and a banner counts the devices that need configuration. Select Configure and answer What type of device is this? Ground Control Station (GCS): a computer running QGroundControl, Mission Planner or similar. It will receive video and telemetry and becomes available for stream bindings. Drone / UAV: a drone with UAVcast-Pro. Choose which paired drone it is, so you can manage its streaming. Select Continue, then Complete Setup.

Danger Zone → Delete Network permanently deletes the VPN network, all connected devices, all authentication keys and all stream bindings. Devices drop off the network, and you'd have to connect every ground station and drone again. Deleting the network also switches VPN off for the organization, and online UAVs are told to leave the VPN. The Network page then shows Enable VPN Network again, which creates a new, empty network. There is no separate switch to turn VPN off: Delete Network is the way to do it.

DeviceNeeds outbound Drone (Fleet Manager connection) HTTPS (TCP 443) to fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com, TCP 8883 for MQTT over TLS Drone and ground station (VPN) HTTPS (TCP 443) to vpn-connect.uavmatrix.com, plus UDP for WireGuard. Tailscale uses UDP 41641 by default. Most cellular and office networks allow this. If devices join the VPN but can't reach each other, see VPN connected but can't reach the drone. When two devices can't reach each other directly over UDP, their traffic is relayed through Tailscale's public DERP relay servers over HTTPS (TCP 443). It stays end-to-end encrypted, but the relay adds delay, so allow outbound UDP where you can.

Route video and MAVLink from any drone to any ground station over VPN, how Fleet Manager assigns UDP ports, and QGC and Mission Planner setup. A stream binding tells a drone to send its video and telemetry to one ground station over your organization's VPN. One drone can stream to several ground stations, and one ground station can receive several drones. Fleet Manager picks the ports so that streams never collide.
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

b: Fleet Manager › Network & VPN › Stream bindings
c: VPN enabled and the drone on the VPN (type UAV in Connected Devices). The ground station connected and configured as GCS. Owner or Admin role. The drone online. Fleet Manager sends the new destinations to UAVcast-Pro right away and waits for it to confirm.

b: Fleet Manager › Network & VPN › Stream bindings
c: Go to Network → Stream Bindings and select Add Binding. In Add Stream Binding, choose the Drone and the Ground Station. Select Create Binding. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/network Add Stream Binding dialog with a drone and a ground station selected, and the note that ports are assigned automatically. The binding appears in the table with Video and Telemetry switched on and its Ports (video / telemetry). UAVcast-Pro starts sending within seconds. If the drone doesn't confirm within 15 seconds, Fleet Manager cancels the binding with Failed to send configuration to drone - it may be offline. Check that the drone is online and try again.

b: Fleet Manager › Network & VPN › Stream bindings
c: Ports are counted per ground station. Each binding gets its own block of UDP ports on that ground station, so drones never overlap: a video port for camera 1, followed by room for camera 2 (dual stream) and audio, which UAVcast-Pro sends to the next ports after the video port; a telemetry port for MAVLink. The first binding on a ground station uses the defaults, video 5600 and telemetry 14550. Later bindings get the next free block. A few consequences worth knowing: Every ground station starts at the defaults. The same drone can have different ports on two laptops, depending on what else each laptop receives. Freed ports are reused. Removing a binding frees its block for the next new binding to that laptop. Ports don't follow the drone. Removing and re-adding a binding can give it different ports. Always read the Ports column before setting up the ground station software. Ports are assigned by Fleet Manager and can't be edited in the app. A Video Port (Camera 2) set by hand on the drone is kept when Fleet Manager updates its destinations only from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3. On earlier versions the next update clears it.

t: Set up the ground station software
b: Fleet Manager › Network & VPN › Stream bindings
c: Use the ports from the binding's Ports column. The stream arrives from the drone's VPN address. QGroundControl Mission Planner Telemetry: QGroundControl listens on UDP 14550 by default, so the first drone connects by itself. For more drones, open Application Settings → Comm Links, add a link of type UDP with the binding's telemetry port, and connect it. Video: in Application Settings → Video (under General in older versions), set Source to UDP h.264 Video Stream and the UDP port to the binding's video port (UDP URL 0.0.0.0:<port> in current versions). QGroundControl shows one video at a time; to watch several drones, run a second instance or use a video player for the others. Telemetry: in the connection drop-down at the top right, choose UDP, select Connect and enter the binding's telemetry port. For several drones, connect once per port; Mission Planner lists each vehicle by system ID. Video: right-click the HUD, choose Video → Set GStreamer Source and enter a pipeline that listens on the binding's video port. See Mission Planner for the exact pipeline. Give each drone its own MAVLink system ID When one ground station receives several drones, each flight controller needs a unique SYSID_THISMAV (ArduPilot) or MAV_SYS_ID (PX4). Otherwise the ground station mixes them up. More on running many vehicles from one station: Stream to multiple ground stations.

b: Fleet Manager › Network & VPN › Stream bindings
c: Switch Video or Telemetry off in the table to stop that stream without losing the binding or its ports. Do this while the drone is online, so it gets the change. Select the trash icon to remove the binding. The ports become free for the next binding to that ground station. How Fleet Manager secures drones with per-drone TLS certificates, isolates organizations on private WireGuard VPNs, enforces roles and stores data. This page is for the people who have to sign off on Fleet Manager: security officers, IT and operations managers.

c: Per-drone client certificates. At pairing, Fleet Manager issues each drone its own TLS client certificate. The drone uses it to connect to Fleet Manager's MQTT broker on port 8883, the broker's only public listener. There is no shared password. Each drone can only use its own topics. The certificate's identity is the drone's device ID, and the broker only lets a drone publish and subscribe under its own topics. One compromised drone can't read or command another. Outbound only. Drones connect out to Fleet Manager. You don't open inbound ports on the drone or its network. Short pairing window. Pairing codes are 8 random digits, valid 5 minutes and usable once. Code checks are rate-limited (10 checks and 5 pairing attempts per user per minute). The drone's certificate and VPN key are only handed out until the drone first connects, and never later than 15 minutes after the code expires. Certificate upgrades. When Fleet Manager tightens the certificate scheme, older drones are flagged Re-pair required instead of being silently trusted.

Each organization gets its own network on Fleet Manager's VPN server (vpn-connect.uavmatrix.com), a self-hosted Tailscale-compatible control server. Traffic between devices is end-to-end encrypted with WireGuard. Devices of one organization can't see another organization's devices: the VPN server enforces a separate access rule for each organization. If Fleet Manager can't confirm that isolation, it hides the auth key (VPN isolation could not be verified, so the auth key is hidden.) instead of handing out a key. Joining needs an auth key that only Owners and Admins can create. Keys expire after 90 days. Drones receive the key automatically during pairing or Push to Drone, and only with an Owner's or Admin's consent. Removing a device in Network removes it from the VPN server.

Sign-in goes through your UAVmatrix account. Fleet Manager stores no passwords. Three roles per organization (Owner, Admin, Viewer), enforced on the server for every action. See Roles and permissions. The SSH terminal and remote access to UAVcast-Pro are limited to Owners and Admins. Invitation links are encrypted, can be used once and expire after 7 days. UAVmatrix can suspend accounts or organizations that break the terms. Suspended users see Account Suspended or Organization Suspended with the reason and a support contact.

DataKept Telemetry (position, altitude, speed, heading, battery, mode, armed state, GPS, service status), once per second Per the organization's retention setting: 7 days to 1 year (default 1 year). Compressed after 7 days. Deleted when the drone is removed. Saved flight names and time ranges Until deleted, or the drone is removed Commands sent to drones, with who sent them Until the drone is removed Activity log (who paired, removed, invited, changed roles) Kept when drones or members are removed Missions Until deleted, or the organization is deleted Support tickets and their screenshots Kept for support Fleet Manager doesn't store video. Video and MAVLink to ground stations travel over the VPN between your devices, and Fleet Manager doesn't record them. The terminal and the remote UAVcast-Pro proxy pass through Fleet Manager's encrypted connection to the drone; their content isn't stored. VPN traffic goes directly between your devices when the networks allow it. When they don't (for example behind strict NAT or a mobile carrier), it falls back to Tailscale's public relay (DERP) servers. The traffic stays end-to-end encrypted with WireGuard either way; UAVmatrix doesn't run a relay.

Maps: map tiles come from Esri; the airspace layer from OpenAIP through Fleet Manager. FleetBot: chat messages are sent to Anthropic to generate answers. Nothing else from your organization is sent. See Support and FleetBot. Product analytics and error reports: Fleet Manager uses PostHog for usage analytics, such as which pages are opened and which buttons are used, and to report app errors.

c: UAVcast-Pro installs on any 64-bit Linux board or PC with an arm64 or amd64 (x86-64) CPU running Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu. 32-bit systems (armv7l, i686) are not supported. BoardStatusNotes Raspberry Pi 5 Supported No hardware H.264 encoder. Video is encoded in software, so watch the System load indicator on the Camera page with high resolutions or two streams. Raspberry Pi 4 Supported, recommended Good balance of CPU, power draw and price. 2 GB RAM or more. Raspberry Pi 3 / 3B+ Supported Fine for telemetry and one 720p stream. Installation takes about 30 minutes. Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W Supported Smallest and lightest. Installation takes about 30 minutes; keep video modest. Raspberry Pi Compute Module 3+/4 Supported Same as the matching Pi model. NVIDIA Jetson, Orange Pi, Banana Pi and other arm64 boards Supported Use the vendor's 64-bit Ubuntu or Debian image. UAVcast-Pro recognises these boards and suggests their serial ports for the flight controller. Use a USB camera (Raspberry Pi CSI cameras need a Pi). x86-64 PC (Intel NUC, mini PC, laptop) Supported Uses the amd64 build. USB serial adapters show up as /dev/ttyUSB* or /dev/ttyACM*. Run uname -m on the board to check the architecture. You want aarch64 or x86_64. Minimum 500 MB free on the root disk, or the installer stops. An 8 GB or larger card is the practical minimum; use 32 GB or more if you record video on the drone. Use a good A1/A2-rated microSD card, or boot from SSD. Recordings can also go to a USB drive or SSD (see Recordings). The license is tied to the storage device UAVcast-Pro identifies a device by its CPU serial number plus the serial number of the boot disk (SD card or SSD). Moving to a new SD card counts as a new device. Unregister the old one first. See Move your license to new hardware.

The Raspberry Pi needs a stable 5.1 V supply that can carry the Pi plus everything on its USB ports. A 4G modem can draw well over 500 mA when it transmits, and a USB camera adds more. Power the Pi from a dedicated 5 V BEC or regulator sized for the whole load. A flight controller's TELEM or USB port cannot power the Pi. If the modem browns out the Pi, power it from a powered USB hub or a separate 5 V supply. Check the Power supply row on the Dashboard. Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply means the Pi is under-voltage right now. Slowed down (heat or power) means the CPU is throttling.

UAVcast-Pro works with any MAVLink flight controller: ArduPilot (Copter, Plane, Rover, Sub) and PX4, on Pixhawk and Cube families, Matek, Holybro, CUAV, mRo and most other boards. On a PX4 flight controller, telemetry, video, routing to ground stations, the map and the HUD work the same way; use your ground station to change PX4 flight modes. Connect it in one of two ways: LinkWiringWhen to use USB USB cable from the flight controller's USB port to the companion computer. Easiest. No baud rate to set. Use a short, good-quality data cable. UART / Serial TELEM port TX → computer RX, RX → computer TX, GND → GND. Or a USB-serial (FTDI) cable. When the USB port is used for something else, or for a cleaner install. Enable MAVLink on that port: SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 2 (MAVLink2) on ArduPilot, MAV_x_CONFIG on PX4. Raspberry Pi only: the GPIO UART is /dev/serial0 (GPIO 14 TX, GPIO 15 RX). The installer frees it for the flight controller: it disables the serial login console and, on Pi 3, 4 and Zero 2 W, moves Bluetooth off the UART. Never connect the flight controller's 5 V pin to the Pi when both have their own supply. On other boards, use the board's UART (for example ttyTHS* on Jetson, ttyS* on Orange Pi) or a USB-serial adapte

The drone checks the license with the UAVmatrix license server every 4 hours. If the server can't be reached, the drone keeps its last known status. You can fly with no internet connection at all; nothing locks while you're offline. A device is identified by its CPU serial number and the serial number of its boot disk (SD card or SSD). Unregistering frees a slot immediately. You can unregister any device on the license from any drone where the license is active, not only the drone you're on. Use this when you replace the Pi, swap the SD card, or move from a test bench to the aircraft. On the old device, go to Application → License Manager and select Unregister next to it. If the old device is dead, unregister it from another drone on the same license, or contact support.

From your store account, open the license and select Upgrade Options: Extend subscription adds another period. If the license is still valid, the new period is added to the current expiry date; if it has expired, it starts on the renewal date. The key stays the same. Add devices adds slots to the license. An expired license must be renewed first. Upgrade tier moves the license to a plan with more slots. The drone picks up the new expiry date and slots at its next check, within 4 hours. To refresh it right away, select Change in License Manager, enter the same key and select Validate.

An expired license locks UAVcast-Pro When a license expires, UAVcast-Pro can no longer be used on any of its drones. It does not keep running on the installed version. When the license server reports the license as expired, the drone marks itself unlicensed: the web interface only opens Application, and telemetry, video, NTRIP and Dynamic DNS stop at the next restart of their services. Renew the license before the expiry date to avoid downtime, and validate the key again on the drone (or wait for its next check, within 4 hours) to unlock it.

UAVcast-Pro turns a Raspberry Pi or Linux companion computer into a 4G/LTE link for MAVLink telemetry and H.264 video. See how it works with Fleet Manager. UAVcast-Pro is software for a companion computer on your drone, usually a Raspberry Pi. It reads MAVLink from any MAVLink flight controller (ArduPilot or PX4), streams H.264 video from one or two cameras, and sends both to your ground control station over Wi-Fi, Ethernet or a 4G/LTE modem. Pair a drone running UAVcast-Pro with Fleet Manager and you can see the whole fleet on one map, open a remote terminal, plan missions and route video and telemetry to ground stations without port forwarding. Fleet Manager is included with every UAVcast-Pro license.

A camera, if you want video. A laptop with QGroundControl or Mission Planner, and the Tailscale client. A Fleet Manager organization where you are Owner or Admin. Rules for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight Flying beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) needs an authorization in most countries. UAVcast-Pro gives you the link; the operational approval, the risk assessment and the fail-safes are your responsibility.

 The drone sends MAVLink and H.264 video to your laptop's VPN address. The VPN makes the laptop reachable over 4G as if both were on the same local network. Prefer to run your own VPN? You can use your own ZeroTier network or Tailscale tailnet instead of Fleet Manager: see VPN and Remote access with Tailscale. Steps 1, 2 and 7 to 9 below stay the same.

b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: Plug the flight controller into the companion computer over USB, or wire a TELEM port (TX→RX, RX→TX, GND→GND) and enable MAVLink on that port (SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 2 on ArduPilot, MAV_x_CONFIG on PX4). In UAVcast-Pro, open Flight Controller → Connection. Choose USB or UART / Serial under Link type, and leave Port and Baud rate on Automatic. Wait for the status Connected and a vehicle in Vehicle. If it stays at No heartbeat, see No MAVLink heartbeat.

b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: Plug in the modem and open Modem. Set Enable cellular Modem? to Yes and pick the Modem type: HiLink for modems that act as a USB network adapter (for example Huawei E3372h), Traditional (PPP) for the rest. For a Traditional modem, leave Access Point Name (Optional) empty. UAVcast-Pro finds the APN for your SIM and remembers it. Under Modem Information, wait for an operator and an IPv4 address. Go to Networks and choose Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode), so traffic leaves over the modem even when Wi-Fi is around. Details: Cellular modem. If the modem connects but nothing loads: Modem connected, no internet.

t: 3. Turn on the VPN in Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: In Fleet Manager, open Network. If it shows Enable VPN Network, select it. This creates your organization's private network. See Network and VPN.

t: 4. Pair the drone and put it on the VPN
b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: In UAVcast-Pro, go to Management → Fleet Management and select Connect to Fleet Manager. Note the 8-digit code. In Fleet Manager, go to Fleet → Pair Device, enter the code and confirm the device. On the VPN Connection step, keep Enable VPN for this UAV ticked and select Complete Pairing. The drone appears under Network → Connected Devices with the UAV type and a 100.x.y.z address. Full walkthrough: Add your first drone to Fleet Manager.

t: 5. Put the laptop on the VPN
b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: Install Tailscale on the laptop. You don't need a Tailscale account: Fleet Manager runs its own VPN server. In Fleet Manager, on Network → Devices, copy the GCS Connection Command under Connect a Device and run it on the laptop as administrator (sudo on macOS and Linux). The laptop appears in Connected Devices. In the Type column, select Configure, choose Ground Control Station (GCS) and select Complete Setup. Test: ping <drone VPN IP> from the laptop. You can now open the drone's web interface at http://<drone VPN IP>/. Details and screenshots: Connect a ground station.

t: 6. Send telemetry and video to the laptop
b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: In Fleet Manager, go to Network → Stream Bindings and select Add Binding. Choose the drone and the laptop, then select Create Binding. Fleet Manager sends the destination to the drone; it appears on the drone's Ground Control Stations page with a cloud icon. Read the binding's video and telemetry ports in the Ports column. For the first drone on a laptop they are the defaults, 5600 and 14550. On the laptop, allow incoming UDP on those ports in the firewall (commands in No video, check 3).

b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: Open Camera → Camera settings, set Enable Camera? to Yes and choose the camera in Select Camera. For LTE, start with Resolution 1280×720, Select FPS 15–20 and Bitrate: around 1000–1500 kbps. Settings save as you change them. Press Start if the camera isn't running yet.

b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: QGroundControl connects to UDP 14550 by itself. For video, set Source to UDP h.264 Video Stream on the binding's video port in the video settings. Mission Planner: choose UDP, press Connect, enter the binding's telemetry port. For video, set the GStreamer source as described on the Mission Planner page.

b: Guides › Fly beyond visual range over 4G
c: Turn off the companion computer's Wi-Fi, or take the drone away from it, so the only path is the modem. Check the dashboard: Cellular connected, VPN connected, Ground station Sending, Video running. Watch the link for 10 minutes on the ground, ideally at the take-off site. Look for video freezes and telemetry gaps. On Flight Controller → Connection, check GCS Failsafe Information. If it shows Warning - Failsafe Disabled, enable the GCS failsafe on the flight controller (ArduPilot: FS_GCS_ENABL on Plane, FS_GCS_ENABLE on Copter; PX4: NAV_DLL_ACT) and choose its action, so the drone acts on its own when the link drops. Record every flight Turn on Record automatically when armed under Camera → Recordings → Settings. You get the video and a telemetry log of every flight for later review: Record flights and review them. UAVnet is being retired UAVnet, UAVmatrix's hosted ZeroTier controller, is being discontinued in favour of Fleet Manager. If your drones use a UAVnet network today, move them to the Fleet Manager VPN as described above.

t: Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
p: Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
c: Connect two cameras to UAVcast-Pro and switch between them from your RC transmitter, or stream both at once with dual stream. Setup, ports and CPU. UAVcast-Pro handles two cameras, for example a forward camera and a downward or zoom camera. You choose between two modes: Switching (default)Dual stream What the ground station gets One video stream, showing camera 1 or camera 2 Two video streams at the same time How you choose The camera badges in the web interface, or an RC channel Both always live Ports Video Port Camera 1 on Video Port, camera 2 on Video Port (Camera 2) (default: Video Port + 1) CPU and bandwidth One encode Two encodes, about double the uplink
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

p: Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
b: Guides › Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
c: Connect both cameras. Two CSI cameras on a Pi 5, a CSI and a USB camera, or two USB cameras all work. Open Camera → Camera settings. The camera slots show CAM 1 and CAM 2. Click Add Camera on the second slot and choose the camera. Resolution and FPS from Camera 1 will be used in switching mode. If camera 2 supports camera 1's resolution, turn on Match Camera 1 Resolution; otherwise camera 2 uses its own resolution and is scaled to match. If a camera is missing from the list, see Camera not detected.

p: Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
b: Guides › Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
c: Under RC Channel Switching, turn on Enable RC channel camera switching. Choose a free channel in RC Channel. The default is channel 7. Map a two-position switch on your transmitter to that channel. Flip the switch and watch Current PWM: below 1500 µs selects camera 1, above 1500 µs selects camera 2. <drone-ip>/camera Camera Control Panel with one camera. The RC Channel Switching panel appears below it only once CAM 2 is added and dual stream is off. While RC switching is on, the camera badges in the web interface don't switch cameras. Turn RC switching off to select cameras by hand again.

p: Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
b: Guides › Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
c: Turn on Dual stream. The badge shows Both live. Each camera now has its own resolution, FPS and bitrate under Per-camera settings. Open Ground Control Stations. Each destination now shows Video Port (Camera 2). Leave it empty to use Video Port + 1 (5601), or enter a port. On the ground station, receive the second stream on that port, for example with a second QGroundControl video source or a GStreamer window: see Ground stations & video for QGroundControl, Mission Planner and GStreamer on every OS. Watch the CPU UAVcast-Pro encodes video in software. With two streams, keep an eye on System load. When it says CPU is near its limit, lower one stream's resolution or bitrate, or turn the second stream off. A Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 is recommended for dual stream. The Flight Map shows one video window per active stream. You can hide them as tabs at the bottom of the map.

p: Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
b: Guides › Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
c: With dual stream on, each destination uses two video ports, and audio (if Send audio to ground stations is on) uses video port + 2. If you add more destinations on the same computer, space their video ports at least three apart, for example 5600 and 5610.

p: Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
b: Guides › Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream
c: Under Camera → Recordings → Settings, Record camera 2 works only when dual stream is on. See Record flights and review them.

t: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: Plan licenses, then name, pair and connect 20+ UAVcast-Pro drones to UAVmatrix Fleet Manager, with team roles, the organization VPN and stream bindings. This guide walks through bringing a fleet of, say, 20 drones into UAVmatrix Fleet Manager in one go: licenses, naming, pairing, the organization VPN, and wiring ground stations to drones. It assumes each drone already runs UAVcast-Pro with its flight controller connected and internet access.
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: Two rules decide whether a drone can be paired: Every drone needs an active UAVcast-Pro license on the device. One license can cover several drones: its Allowed Devices count is the number of slots. For 20 drones you need 20 slots in total, across one or more licenses. The license must be owned by a member of the organization you pair into. Fleet Manager matches the e-mail address of the store account that bought the license with the members' e-mail addresses. If purchasing bought the licenses under another account, invite that account to the organization, or ask support to add the purchasing e-mail to your user. Check this before the pairing day: a drone whose license belongs to an outsider is refused with License is not owned by any member of this organization.

t: 2. Set up the organization and team
p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: Sign in to fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com with your uavmatrix.com account and create the organization. See Set up an organization. Under Team, invite your people. Owners and Admins can pair, control and remove drones; Viewers can only watch. See Roles and permissions. Split the pairing work between two or three Admins if you have many drones. Each user can complete 5 pairings per minute; the limit stops brute-force guessing, and also slows down one person pairing 20 drones back to back.

p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: The name a drone has in UAVcast-Pro becomes its name in Fleet Manager. Agree on a pattern, for example SURVEY-01 … SURVEY-20, and label the airframes to match. On each drone, open UAVcast-Pro → Fleet Management and fill in Device Name. Without a name the drone appears with its hostname. You can rename it in Fleet Manager later.

p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: Repeat for every drone. With two browser windows side by side (the drone's UAVcast-Pro and Fleet Manager), each takes about a minute. In UAVcast-Pro, open Fleet Management and press Connect to Fleet Manager. An 8-digit Pairing Code appears. It expires after 5 minutes. In Fleet Manager, go to Fleet → Pair Device. Select Organization, then Enter Pairing Code. Confirm Device: check the name, hostname, architecture and UAVcast version, so you pair the drone you think you are pairing. VPN Connection: tick Enable VPN for this UAV if ground stations should reach the drone over the organization's VPN. If the drone already uses Tailscale, Replace existing VPN with Fleet Manager network moves it to the organization's network. Complete Pairing. In UAVcast-Pro, Fleet Connection changes to Connected. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/pair-device Fleet → Pair Device, Confirm Device step. Errors and what they mean: Pairing code invalid or expired. The full wizard is described in Pair your first UAV.

p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: Open Fleet. Every drone should be listed as online. On Fleet Map, each drone appears at its GPS position once its flight controller has a fix. A drone that shows Offline has not reported for 20 seconds: see Drone offline in Fleet Manager.

p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: Go to Network and press Enable VPN Network if the organization's VPN is not on yet. Press Connect a Device, choose Ground Control Station (GCS) and copy the GCS Connection Command. Run it in a terminal on the ground station laptop, with Tailscale installed. Do not paste it into UAVcast-Pro. The laptop appears under Ground Stations once it is connected. Under Stream Bindings, press Add Stream Binding and link each drone to the ground station that should receive it. The drone must be online, because Fleet Manager pushes the destination to it. Each binding gets its own block of ports on that ground station: the first drone uses the defaults, 5600 (video) and 14550 (telemetry), and each further drone gets the next free block. Set up the ground station software with the ports shown on each binding. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/network Network → Stream Bindings: each binding shows its ground station and its video and telemetry ports. Details: Connect a ground station and Stream bindings. Dual stream and audio Each binding gets its own block of ports on the ground station, with room for the drone's second camera and audio after its video port, so several drones can share one ground station.

p: Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
b: Guides › Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager
c: Re-pair required: when Fleet Manager shows this badge, re-pair the drone once from UAVcast-Pro. It keeps its name and history. See Remove or transfer a UAV. Replacing a drone's SD card or board frees nothing by itself: unregister the old device under Application → License Manager → Activated Devices on any drone that uses the same license, then pair the new one. Remote work on a drone: the UAV details page in Fleet Manager has a terminal, logs and actions such as reboot. See UAV details.

Send telemetry and live video from one drone to several QGroundControl or Mission Planner stations with UAVcast-Pro, with read-only observers. One drone, several screens: a pilot on Mission Planner, a payload operator on QGroundControl, a supervisor watching from the office. UAVcast-Pro sends telemetry and video to every destination you add, each with its own switches.
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

b: Guides › Stream to multiple ground stations
c: Each entry under Ground Control Stations is one destination: an IPv4 address plus a telemetry port and a video port. UAVcast-Pro sends: MAVLink telemetry over UDP to Telemetry Port (default 14550) when Enable Telemetry is on, H.264 video over RTP/UDP to Video Port (default 5600) when Enable Video is on, nothing at all when Enable Endpoint is off. Commands from every destination reach the flight controller, unless that destination is Read Only.

b: Guides › Stream to multiple ground stations
c: Open Ground Control Stations and press Add Destination once for each station. Give each a Name you will recognize in the field, for example Pilot – Mission Planner and Payload – QGC. Enter each computer's IPv4 address in Destination IP or Host. Over 4G, use VPN addresses. Switch on Enable Telemetry and Enable Video where they are needed. A station that only needs telemetry saves bandwidth with video off. <drone-ip>/ground-control Ground Control Station with two destination cards. Add Destination adds one card per station.

b: Guides › Stream to multiple ground stations
c: For anyone who should watch but never fly, switch on Read Only on their destination. The station still receives live telemetry, but it can't change anything on the vehicle: commands, mode changes, arming, parameter writes, mission writes and RC overrides from it are blocked. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes. Ground station software may show warnings in this mode, because some of its requests (such as downloading parameters or the mission) go unanswered. Two pilots, one drone Without Read Only, every station can command the drone. Agree who flies, and make every other station read-only.

b: Guides › Stream to multiple ground stations
c: Two programs on one computer can't listen on the same port. Add two destinations with the same IP and different ports, for example: DestinationTelemetry PortVideo Port Mission Planner 14550 5600 QGroundControl 14551 5603 Then set the second program to listen on those ports (in QGroundControl, add a UDP comm link on 14551 and set the video UDP port to 5603). Space video ports 3 apart (5600, 5603, 5606 …). Each destination uses its video port, plus video port + 1 for the second camera in dual stream and video port + 2 for audio. Ports closer together collide as soon as you turn on dual stream or audio.

b: Guides › Stream to multiple ground stations
c: Every video destination is a separate copy of the stream. Three video destinations at 1500 kbps need about 4.5 Mbit/s of uplink from the drone. Over 4G, send video only to the stations that need it, or lower the bitrate on Camera → Camera settings. Dashboard → Network Traffic shows what the modem actually sends.

t: 5. Check that every station gets data
b: Guides › Stream to multiple ground stations
c: On Dashboard, the Ground station row shows Sending to n · x packets/s. The Connection check on Flight Controller → Connection lists each ground station output, and any destination left out because its address is invalid.

b: Guides › Stream to multiple ground stations
c: In Fleet Manager, ground stations join the organization's VPN and you connect them to drones with Stream Bindings on the Network page. Each additional drone bound to the same ground station gets its own block of ports. See Stream bindings.

Record camera video and telemetry on the drone automatically when armed, store it on USB or SSD, and replay video, map and flight data on one timeline. Since v6.5.1, UAVcast-Pro records on the drone itself: camera video plus a telemetry log, with one click on the flight map or automatically every time you arm. Recording reuses the stream that is already encoded, so it costs no extra CPU and never interrupts the live video to the ground station. Afterwards, the flight review player shows the video, the map track, the cockpit view and the flight data on one timeline.
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

b: Guides › Record flights and review them
c: Plug in a USB drive or SSD if you want to record to it. Recordings fill storage fast, and a USB SSD is more robust than an SD card. Open Camera → Recordings and the Settings tab. Under Storage location, pick the disk, or Internal storage. Press Look for disks again if the drive was plugged in after the page opened. Or another folder lets you enter a path and confirm with Use this folder. Set Keep free (default 2 GB). Recording never fills the disk beyond this. <drone-ip>/camera Camera → Recordings → Settings with Internal storage selected and Record automatically when armed on.

b: Guides › Record flights and review them
c: SettingDefaultWhat it does Record automatically when armed On Starts when the motors arm and stops when they disarm. If the link drops in flight, recording carries on. Record camera 1 / Record camera 2 On Camera 2 only records when dual stream is on. Delete oldest recordings when space runs low On Works like a dashcam: recording never stops for lack of space. When off, recording stops instead. Delete recordings older than 0 days 0 keeps recordings until the space is needed. File length 1 min Recordings are saved in pieces of 1–30 minutes. Shorter pieces lose less after a power cut. Record telemetry While armed Always while connected also logs on the ground, starting a new file at every arm, disarm and hour. Off records video only.

b: Guides › Record flights and review them
c: On the Flight Map, the Recording buttons start and stop each camera (Record camera 1, Stop recording camera 1) and the telemetry log. Read-only users can watch but can't start recordings.

b: Guides › Record flights and review them
c: Open Camera → Recordings → Library. Every flight is listed with its video, a thumbnail and its telemetry. A recording in progress shows a Rec badge. <drone-ip>/camera Camera → Recordings → Library with two recorded flights, each with camera video and telemetry. From the library you can: Play a flight in the flight review player, Download video clips as MP4, Delete a recording: Delete video only, or Delete video and telemetry.

b: Guides › Record flights and review them
c: The flight review player plays the video next to the map track, the cockpit view and the flight data (Altitude, Speed, Battery, Satellites, Mode) on one timeline. <drone-ip>/camera Flight review player: video, map and cockpit view above one timeline. The timeline marks arm, disarm and flight-mode changes, so you can jump to the moment that matters. Use Back 10 seconds and Forward 10 seconds, and Playback speed from 0.5× to 4×. With two cameras, Change video layout switches between Picture in picture and Side by side; Show this camera large swaps them. If a recording has no telemetry, the player says No telemetry log for this recording. Telemetry is logged while the drone is armed.

b: Guides › Record flights and review them
c: Recordings are stored on the drone. Download what you need to keep before Delete oldest recordings when space runs low removes it. The dashboard's Storage card and the Recording storage summary show free space. Recording continues with Enable Live Preview? switched off. If the recording service stops responding, the page says The recording service is not responding. Restart the camera service from Camera → Camera settings and collect logs if it happens again.

Reach your drone over LTE with Tailscale and UAVcast-Pro, no port forwarding: log in by URL or auth key, add the laptop as a GCS, stop key expiry. Tailscale is a WireGuard-based VPN. If your team already uses it, it is the quickest way to reach a drone over 4G: the drone and your laptop join the same tailnet and talk to each other on their 100.x.y.z addresses. Don't have a tailnet? The Fleet Manager VPN, included with your license, does the same without a Tailscale account: see Fly beyond visual range over 4G and Onboard a fleet. You need: UAVcast-Pro with internet on the drone (Wi-Fi or modem), a Tailscale account, and the Tailscale client on your laptop.
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

t: 1. Log the drone in to Tailscale
c: In UAVcast-Pro, open Virtual Private Network. Set Enable VPN to Yes and Services to Tailscale. Choose how to log in: Web Login: press Generate Login URL, then Authenticate this device and log in with your Tailscale account in the page that opens. Auth Key: create an auth key in the Tailscale admin console, paste it into Auth Key, optionally set Hostname (Optional), and press Connect with Auth Key. Use this when you set up drones for someone else, or many at once. Wait for Connected. Note the IPv4 Address (100.x.y.z). <drone-ip>/private-network Virtual Private Network with Services set to Tailscale, before the drone is logged in (Not Connected). After login, VPN Information shows the connection details. Turn off key expiry for drones Tailscale device keys expire, and a drone with an expired key drops off the tailnet until someone logs it in again. The Expires field shows when. In the Tailscale admin console, disable key expiry for drones you deploy.

t: 2. Put the laptop on the same tailnet
c:
Install Tailscale on the laptop and log in with the same account or tailnet. Run tailscale status: the drone must be in the list. Then: Terminal
ping <drone tailscale ip>
 Open the drone's web interface at http:///.

t: 3. Send telemetry and video to the laptop
c: In UAVcast-Pro, go to Ground Control Stations and press Add Destination. In Destination IP or Host, enter the laptop's Tailscale IPv4 address (run tailscale ip -4 on the laptop). Switch on Enable Telemetry and Enable Video. Allow incoming UDP 14550 and 5600 on the laptop's firewall. Windows often treats the Tailscale adapter as a public network. Open QGroundControl or Mission Planner. Telemetry arrives on UDP 14550 and video on UDP 5600.

The Relay field on the Virtual Private Network page shows whether traffic goes through a Tailscale relay. A relayed path works but adds delay. Some cellular carriers don't allow direct connections, so test on the carrier you fly with.

Can't ping the drone: VPN connected but can't reach the drone Ping works, no telemetry: No telemetry in the ground station If the drone is later paired with Fleet Manager and you choose Replace existing VPN with Fleet Manager network, it leaves your tailnet and joins the organization's network.

t: RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
p: RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
c:
Stream RTCM3 corrections from an NTRIP caster over LTE to your flight controller with UAVcast-Pro for RTK Fixed, with no base station on site. UAVcast-Pro can pull RTCM3 corrections from an NTRIP caster over the drone's own internet link and pass them to the flight controller. You get RTK Float or RTK Fixed positioning without carrying a base station or a separate radio. Any standard NTRIP v1 or v2 caster works. Text
NTRIP caster ──RTCM3 over TCP/TLS──► UAVcast-Pro ──MAVLink GPS_RTCM_DATA──► flight controller ──► RTK GPS
▲ │
└──────── GGA position (VRS) ────────┘
 You need: An RTK-capable GPS on the flight controller, such as a u-blox F9P module, Here3+ or Septentrio Mosaic. Standard M8N/M10 navigation modules can't do RTK. UAVcast-Pro with the flight controller Connected and internet on the drone. A caster account: a national CORS network, a commercial service (Trimble, Hexagon, Topcon …) or the free community caster rtk2go.com.

p: RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
b: Guides › RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
c: Open Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK. Enter Caster host and Port (usually 2101). Turn on Use TLS (HTTPS) only if your provider requires it. Commercial casters often do, public ones rarely. Enter Username and Password. For rtk2go.com, use your e-mail address as the username and leave the password empty. Press Test connection. Wait for Caster accepted the credentials.

p: RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
b: Guides › RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
c: Press Browse mountpoints. UAVcast-Pro loads the caster's list. Pick the mountpoint closest to where you fly. The list shows Format, GNSS, Country, Location and whether it needs a position (NMEA: Required). Press Select. The name lands in Mountpoint. <drone-ip>/flight-controller The Caster card. Browse mountpoints, next to the Mountpoint field, opens the list of mountpoints.

t: 3. Send your position (VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters)
p: RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
b: Guides › RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
c: VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters build corrections for your location, so they need your position as an NMEA GGA sentence. Leave Send GGA upstream on (the default) with Send interval (seconds) at 10. Keep Position source on Live position from flight controller. Enter Latitude, Longitude and Altitude (m) under the manual position as well. UAVcast-Pro uses it until the flight controller has a GPS fix. For a single fixed base, GGA does no harm, but you can turn it off.

p: RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
b: Guides › RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
c: Turn on Enable NTRIP client. Within seconds the status panel should show: Status: Streaming corrections, with Caster response like ICY 200 OK. RTCM messages forwarded climbing and Last RTCM frame at just now. Recent message types with your constellations, for example 1005, 1077, 1087, 1097. The RTK fix badge moving from 3D fix to RTK Float and then RTK Fixed under open sky. <drone-ip>/flight-controller The status panel and GPS quality card, shown here before a caster is set up (Disabled, no GPS fix). Once corrections flow, these are the fields to watch. The GPS quality card adds the receiver's reported accuracy and a measured Position stability (1σ) that doesn't rely on the receiver's own estimate. The dashboard shows the state under RTK corrections and the fix type under GPS.

p: RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster
