c: Fixed: enabling the camera could show "Insufficient permissions". Fixed: the camera stopped when the live preview was switched off while recording was on. Video to the ground station now keeps running, and preview and recording come back by themselves when the video server is available again. Fixed: the camera service could hang after an automatic video restart until the service was restarted.

New Camera recording: record camera 1 and camera 2 with one click from the flight map, or automatically while the drone is armed. Recording uses the stream that is already encoded, so it costs no extra CPU and never interrupts the live video to the ground station. Storage management: record to the internal disk or a USB drive or SSD, keep a free-space reserve, and remove the oldest recordings automatically before the disk fills up (or stop recording instead). Camera → Recordings page: every flight with its video and telemetry, thumbnails, a live badge while recording, MP4 downloads, and delete (video only, or video and telemetry). Flight review player: a flight's video together with the map track, the cockpit view and the flight data on one timeline, with arm/disarm and flight-mode markers, 0.5×–4× speed and two-camera layouts. Record telemetry setting: while armed (default), always while connected, or off. ARM / DISARM button on the flight map, always behind a confirmation. The flight controller's own safety checks still decide. Messages list on the flight map: every flight controller message, with the current pre-arm problems shown separately. Messages that arrive in bursts are no longer lost. Automatic APN: leave the APN empty and UAVcast-Pro finds the right one for your SIM and remembers it. Improved Clear mission now deletes the mission from the flight controller and waits

New camera audio: sound from a USB microphone or a USB camera's built-in microphone, encoded as Opus. The camera's own microphone is picked automatically when it has one. Audio is carried in the live preview (unmute the player to hear it) and can be sent to every ground station as a separate RTP/Opus stream on Video Port + 2 for GStreamer or VLC receivers. New audio indicator on the Camera page: live level meter, the active device, and a plain-language reason if audio could not start. A failing microphone never interrupts video. Selecting a camera that cannot deliver the configured resolution no longer stops video: the stream falls back to the largest supported size and the log says which resolution to pick. A fatal video error now restarts the pipeline automatically. Faster NTRIP/RTK recovery: after a brief internet drop, corrections resume within seconds instead of up to about 18 minutes. A silent caster connection is detected within 15 s and reconnected. Telemetry toggle now fully controls access: the telemetry router no longer accepts TCP connections on port 5760, so a ground station with telemetry disabled gets no data. If you connected over TCP 5760, add your PC as a ground station and connect over UDP. Turning off Enable Endpoint on a ground station now also stops its video and audio, not just telemetry. The flight map's Light and Dark layers no longer show "API key requ

Flight controller connection rebuilt for reliability: the link reconnects by itself after a flight controller reboot, a USB glitch or a late power-up. New automatic port and baud rate (the default, also after upgrading): UAVcast-Pro finds the flight controller, remembers what worked and follows it if the device name changes. New Auto-detect button and live Connection check on the Flight Controller page, showing step by step whether the device is found, data is arriving and telemetry reaches each ground station, with a plain-language fix for the first problem found. Telemetry and video start at power-on without waiting for internet and begin streaming as soon as the connection is up, however long the modem takes. Redesigned dashboard status card with an overall health summary, GPS fix type, battery, cellular signal, ground station traffic and a power supply (undervoltage) warning. Log downloads now include a diagnostics.txt snapshot (settings, serial ports, power and USB events). Controller type selection removed (ArduPilot only); connection settings apply instantly without a restart.

More reliable installs on low-power boards (Pi Zero 2 W), with a realistic time estimate. Complete, persistent logging across all services, bundled into the downloadable log archive, and clearer flight controller connection logging. Fixed: a missing or invalid destination IP address could break the flight controller connection. Such addresses are now rejected in the UI and skipped by the telemetry router.

New dual camera streaming: stream two cameras at the same time, each with its own resolution, FPS and bitrate. New CPU load indicator on the Camera page, which warns when software H.264 encoding nears the limit. The flight map shows a video window per active stream, which you can hide as tabs at the bottom of the map. The installer resolves the renamed camera packages (rpicam-apps → rpicam-apps-core) and GStreamer plugins, fixing installs on newer Raspberry Pi OS and Debian. CSI streaming falls back to a GStreamer x264 pipeline when rpicam-apps lacks H.264 support (Raspberry Pi OS Lite / Debian trixie on Pi 5). Multi-camera and dual stream start reliably on every supported OS, with automatic recovery if the stream stalls. Unsupported resolutions no longer stop the camera from starting (including Match Camera 1 Resolution): capture falls back and the output is scaled.

New Data Streams page: custom telemetry dashboards with charts, gauges, sparklines and numeric tiles bound to any MAVLink value or NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT signal. Multiple boards, drag-and-resize layout, history kept across page reloads. New Telemetry Injectors (Flight Controller → Injectors): feed external sensor data into the MAVLink stream over HTTP, UDP or serial as NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT / NAMED_VALUE_INT. Listeners start at boot without the web interface open. New NTRIP / RTK tab: connect to an NTRIP caster, browse its mountpoints and stream RTCM corrections to the flight controller, including TLS casters. Thanks to Bobby Russell for the feature request and feedback from his high-altitude balloon flights, which inspired Data Streams and injectors.

How many bits per second the video encoder produces. It has to fit inside the uplink of your connection, with headroom.
A camera on the Raspberry Pi's ribbon-cable connector, such as Camera Module 3.

Streaming two cameras to the ground station at the same time, on two video ports.
UAVmatrix's web dashboard for monitoring and controlling many UAVcast-Pro drones in one organization.
The software, and the computer it runs on, that you use to monitor and command the drone: QGroundControl, Mission Planner, MAVProxy.
A flight controller setting that makes the drone act on its own (return, land, loiter) when it stops hearing the ground station.
An NMEA sentence with your position. VRS and nearest-mountpoint NTRIP casters need it to compute corrections for your location.
The video compression format UAVcast-Pro sends. Every common ground station can decode it.
The MAVLink message a flight controller sends about once per second to say "I'm here". No heartbeat means the link carries no readable MAVLink.
A USB modem with a built-in router that connects by itself and appears to Linux as a network adapter.
A UAVcast-Pro listener (HTTP, UDP or serial) that turns your own sensor values into MAVLink NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT messages.
A complete video frame the decoder can start from. More frequent keyframes recover faster from packet loss. Set with Stream Recovery Rate.
The messaging protocol between flight controllers and ground stations.
A named correction stream on an NTRIP caster, usually tied to one base station or a VRS service.
The messaging protocol drones use to talk to Fleet Manager, encrypted with TLS on port 8883.
A protocol, and the server, for streaming GNSS corrections over the internet.
The 8-digit code UAVcast-Pro shows when you connect a drone to Fleet Manager. Valid for 5 minutes, once.

A ground station destination that receives telemetry but can't change anything on the vehicle: commands, mode changes, parameter and mission writes from it are blocked. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes.
A UAVcast-Pro user role that can view pages but can't change settings or control the drone.
The standard message format for GNSS corrections.
Real-time kinematic positioning with corrections. Float is an approximate solution; Fixed is the centimetre-level solution.
The transport UAVcast-Pro uses for video and telemetry: fast, no retransmissions, which keeps latency low.
ArduPilot parameters that set what a serial port speaks (2 = MAVLink2) and how fast.
In Fleet Manager, a link that sends one drone's video and telemetry to one ground station on its own ports.
MAVLink system ID (which vehicle) and component ID (which part of it). The flight controller is usually sysid 1, compid 1.
A private Tailscale network.
A WireGuard-based VPN. UAVcast-Pro can join your tailnet, or the Fleet Manager organization network.
UAVmatrix's hosted ZeroTier network controller at uavnet.uavmatrix.com. It is being discontinued in favour of the Fleet Manager VPN; existing users should move to Fleet Manager.
A correction service that computes corrections for your position from a network of base stations. Needs GGA upstream.
A peer-to-peer VPN. UAVcast-Pro can join your own ZeroTier network.

Power off the Pi. Re-seat the ribbon cable at both ends with the contacts facing the right way, and close the connector latches. A Pi 5 and a Pi Zero 2 W need the narrower 22-pin cable. Boot and run this on the Pi: Terminal
rpicam-hello --list-cameras
 On older Raspberry Pi OS images the command is libcamera-hello --list-cameras. If the camera is not listed here, Linux can't see it. Try another cable or camera before changing anything in UAVcast-Pro. If it is listed, restart the camera from the Camera page (Restart, or Stop then Start) and open Select Camera again. Each CSI camera appears as its own entry, for example CSI Camera 0 - imx708 (libcamera). Two CSI cameras For two cameras the camera driver needs more memory. t: Check 2: CSI camera on Ubuntu or Debian
c: UAVcast-Pro uses rpicam-vid for CSI cameras. The installer installs rpicam-apps (or rpicam-apps-core) on Raspberry Pi OS and Debian. On Ubuntu the Raspberry Pi camera stack is not packaged, and the log says CSI camera not available: Ubuntu requires building libcamera from source. USB cameras are supported. Use Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit if you need a CSI camera, or use a USB camera on Ubuntu.

Plug the camera straight into the companion computer, not through an unpowered hub. Run: Terminal
v4l2-ctl --list-devices
 If the camera is missing, Linux does not see it. Check lsusb and try another port and cable. If it is listed, restart the camera with Restart on the Camera page and open Select Camera again. Most UVC webcams work, for example Logitech C920 and C615. Cameras that only output a format the encoder can't take, or devices that are not video capture devices (some capture cards), are not listed.

t: Check 4: Listed, but video doesn't start

t: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
p: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
c: Fix stuttering, grey smears and lag in UAVcast-Pro video over LTE or VPN by matching bitrate, resolution, FPS and Stream Recovery Rate to the link. The picture arrives, but it stutters, freezes, smears grey blocks across the screen or runs seconds behind. Almost always the stream asks for more than the link can carry, or the encoder sends keyframes too rarely to recover from lost packets. What you seeLikely causeStart at Grey or green smears that clear up after a second or two Packets lost and too few keyframes to recover Check 2 Smooth on Wi-Fi, stutters or freezes over LTE Bitrate above what the cellular uplink carries Check 1 Stutters even on the local network CPU limit on the drone, or the GCS can not decode fast enough Check 3 Video is seconds behind the drone You are looking at the browser preview, or the GCS buffers Check 4
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

t: Check 1: Lower the bitrate and resolution
p: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
c: A cellular uplink is much slower than its download speed and changes as the drone moves between cells. Start low and step up. Go to Camera → Camera settings. Set Resolution to 1280×720 or lower. Set Select FPS to 15 or 20. Move the Bitrate: slider to about 1000–1500 kbps. 0 means auto. Settings save as you change them, and the camera picks them up. Fly, or drive, the route you care about. If it holds up, raise one value at a time. <drone-ip>/camera Camera → Camera Settings: Resolution, Select FPS, Bitrate and Stream Recovery Rate are the values to tune for the uplink. How much does the link carry? Dashboard → Network Traffic shows the live TX rate per interface. If the modem interface sits at the same ceiling whatever bitrate you set, that ceiling is your uplink.

t: Check 2: Set a faster Stream Recovery Rate
p: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
c: Grey overlays come from lost packets. The decoder can only repair the picture at the next keyframe. Stream Recovery Rate sets how often keyframes are sent. In Camera → Camera settings, find Stream Recovery Rate. Move the slider from Auto towards Ultra Fast: fewer frames between keyframes repair the picture sooner but use more bandwidth. Towards Bandwidth Saver saves bandwidth but recovers slowly. The hint under the slider (for example VPN/WiFi Friendly) tells you what each position suits. Save, and compare. If the link is very slow, combine a faster recovery rate with a lower bitrate (check 1). On Auto, UAVcast-Pro sends one keyframe per second (one every FPS frames, or every 30 frames when FPS is on auto).

t: Check 3: Look at the CPU load
p: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
c: UAVcast-Pro encodes H.264 in software. On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, or with two cameras streaming at once, the CPU can run out. Open Camera → Camera settings and look at the System load card. If it says CPU is near its limit. Lower the resolution or bitrate., do exactly that. With Dual stream on, lower one stream's resolution or bitrate, or turn the second stream off. Check Dashboard for Slowed down (heat or power) under Power supply. A throttled CPU encodes slower. See Undervoltage and throttling.

t: Check 4: Know which stream you are watching
p: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
c: The Live Preview in the browser and the video window on the Flight Map go through the built-in media server, which adds delay. They are for setup, not for flying. The stream to your ground station goes straight over UDP and has much lower latency. If the ground station itself lags: In QGroundControl, check that low-latency mode is on in the video settings. In GStreamer pipelines, use sync=false on the video sink, as in the test command. Over VPN, make sure ZeroTier or Tailscale reaches the drone directly and not through a relay. Tailscale shows the relay in use under Relay on the Virtual Private Network page.

p: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
c: Go to Modem and look at Signal Quality and Technology under Modem Information. A weak signal, or a fall back from LTE to 3G, cuts the uplink. Move the modem away from the flight controller, ESCs and power wires, or use a modem with external antennas.

p: Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G
c: Download the logs (Camera Server, last 30 minutes) and send them to support@uavmatrix.com with your camera model, resolution, FPS, bitrate and the kind of link you fly on. Related: Camera settings · Cellular modem

t: Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
p: Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
c: Paired UAV shows Offline or Re-pair required in Fleet Manager? Check the drone's internet, outbound port 8883, UAVcast-Pro Fleet Management and the license. The UAV is paired, but Fleet Manager shows it as Offline (grey on the fleet map), its telemetry is frozen, or it carries a Re-pair required badge. Fleet Manager marks a UAV offline when it has heard nothing from it for 20 seconds. The drone talks to Fleet Manager over an encrypted MQTT connection, on its own internet connection. What you seeLikely causeStart at Offline, and UAVcast-Pro Fleet Management says Disconnected The drone has no internet, or port 8883 is blocked Check 1 Re-pair required badge, or This UAV must be re-paired The drone has an old certificate Check 2 Offline right after you reinstalled or reset UAVcast-Pro The pairing was removed on the drone Check 3 Online, but no position or battery Flight controller not connected to UAVcast-Pro Check 4

t: Check 1: The drone's connection to Fleet Manager
p: Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
c: Open UAVcast-Pro on the drone and go to Fleet Management. Fleet Connection shows Connected or Disconnected, and Last Connected. If it is Disconnected, check that the drone has internet: the dashboard's Cellular row, or curl -I https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com on the device. Fix the link first with Modem connected, no internet. The drone must be able to open an outbound TCP connection on port 8883 (MQTT over TLS). Some company networks, public Wi-Fi and a few IoT SIM plans only allow web ports. Try another network or ask the provider to open 8883. Check the date and time on the device with date. The connection uses certificates, which fail on a device with a wrong clock. Make sure the license on the drone is still active (Application → License Manager).

p: Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
c: Fleet Manager changed how drones connect, and UAVs paired before that change must be paired once more. Nothing is lost: the UAV keeps its name and history, and you don't need to remove it in Fleet Manager. In UAVcast-Pro on the drone, open Fleet Management and press Disconnect from Fleet, then confirm. Press Connect to Fleet Manager. An 8-digit Pairing Code appears with a countdown. In Fleet Manager, go to Fleet → Pair Device, choose the organization and enter the code.

t: Check 3: The drone lost its pairing
p: Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
c: A reinstall with a database reset, Reset Database or Disconnect from Fleet removes the pairing on the drone, so it stops reporting. Pair it again as in check 2. Pairing into the same organization reuses the existing UAV entry.

p: Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager

t: Do I need an LTE modem?
c: No. UAVcast-Pro works over any IP connection: 4G/LTE, Wi-Fi or Ethernet. A modem is what lets you fly beyond Wi-Fi range. Many operators test on Wi-Fi and switch to the modem before flight with Networks → Network Priority → Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode).

Any 64-bit Linux board or PC on arm64 or amd64 running Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, 3, 4 and 5, NVIDIA Jetson, Orange Pi and x86 mini PCs. A Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 is the comfortable choice for video. See Supported hardware.

Any flight controller that speaks MAVLink over USB or a TELEM port: ArduPilot (Copter, Plane, Rover, VTOL and the other vehicle types) and PX4, on Pixhawk and Cube family boards, Matek and similar. Telemetry, video and routing to ground stations work with any of them. The flight-mode buttons in the Flight Map and in Fleet Manager use ArduPilot's mode names; with PX4, change modes from your ground station.

t: Can I connect over the flight controller's USB port?
c: Yes, and it is the simplest option: plug it in and leave Port on Automatic. Use a short cable that carries data. See No MAVLink heartbeat if it isn't found.

Any software that takes MAVLink over UDP, including QGroundControl, Mission Planner and MAVProxy. Video is H.264 over RTP/UDP, which QGroundControl and Mission Planner play directly. GStreamer and VLC work too: see Ground stations & video.

t: Can several ground stations watch at the same time?
c: Yes. Add one destination per computer under Ground Control Stations, each with its own switches for video and telemetry. Use Read Only for stations that should only watch. See Stream to multiple ground stations.

By default telemetry goes to UDP 14550 and video to UDP 5600 on each ground station; a second camera uses the video port + 1, and audio the video port + 2. The web interface is on port 80. The full list is in Ports and protocols.

t: Do I need port forwarding on my router?
c: No. Over 4G, put the drone and the ground station on the same VPN: the Fleet Manager VPN (included with your license), or your own Tailscale or ZeroTier network. The drone sends telemetry and video to the ground station's VPN address. See Fly beyond visual range over 4G.

t: Can I still connect over TCP 5760?
c: No. Since v6.5.0, TCP 5760 is closed so only the ground stations you add get data. Add your computer as a destination and use UDP.

Yes. The flight controller link, telemetry and video start at power-on without waiting for internet, so a local Wi-Fi network or radio link works. Activating the license needs internet once. After that, a failed license check because of a lost connection does not disable the device.
You need a UAVcast-Pro license to activate the drone. Buy one in the UAVmatrix store. Buy UAVcast-ProSee plans and pricing

t: My license won't activate. What now?
c: See License won't activate. The usual causes are a mistyped key, no free device slot, or no internet on the device.

t: What happens when my license expires?
c: UAVcast-Pro is locked: the web interface only opens Application, and telemetry, video and the other services stop until you renew. Renew in the store before the expiry date, then validate the key on the drone. See When a license expires.

t: Is Fleet Manager included with my license?
c: Yes. Fleet Manager, including its VPN, is included with your UAVcast-Pro license at no extra cost.

t: I replaced the SD card. Do I need a new license?
c: No, but the device counts as new and takes a slot. Unregister the old entry under Application → License Manager → Activated Devices.

t: Is Fleet Manager a separate product?
c: Fleet Manager is UAVmatrix's web dashboard for managing many drones at fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com. It is included with your UAVcast-Pro license. You sign in with your uavmatrix.com account, and each drone you pair needs an active UAVcast-Pro license owned by a member of your organization. See Fleet Manager.

t: How do I pair a drone with Fleet Manager?
c: In UAVcast-Pro, open Fleet Management and press Connect to Fleet Manager. Enter the 8-digit code in Fleet Manager under Fleet → Pair Device within 5 minutes. See Pair your first UAV and, if it fails, Pairing code invalid or expired.
Go to Application → Update Application, pick a version in Select version to update and press Update Now. If the card shows Pending Restart, press Restart Now. You can also run the installer again.

t: Can I import settings from v4 or v5?
c: No. v6 uses a new database, so set it up again after a fresh install. Within v6, use Application → Database → Backup Database and Restore Database to move settings between installs.
Yes, since v6.5.1. It records camera 1 and 2 from the flight map, or automatically while the drone is armed, together with a telemetry log. See Record flights and review them.

t: Where does UAVcast-Pro keep its files?
c: Under /opt/uavcast-pro: the database uavcast.db, logs/, recordings/ and missions/. See Services and files.

There is no password reset in the web interface. Another admin can delete your user under Users and create it again. If you were the only admin, recovery isn't self-service: contact support@uavmatrix.com with the details listed in Forgot the admin password.

You ran curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash and it stopped with an error, hung, or finished without a working web interface. c:
UAVcast-Pro v6 needs a 64-bit OS: arm64 or amd64 (x86 PCs). On arm64, boards other than a Raspberry Pi (Jetson and other ARM boards) need UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3 or later; older installers stop with Device is not a Raspberry Pi. Terminal
dpkg --print-architecture # must print arm64 or amd64
uname -m # aarch64 or x86_64
 If you see armhf, armv7l or i686, you are on a 32-bit OS. Flash Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit) with Raspberry Pi Imager and install again. Supported systems are Raspberry Pi OS, Debian and Ubuntu; see Supported hardware.

The installer downloads UAVcast-Pro and system packages, and installs ZeroTier and Tailscale. Check internet access: curl -I https://install.uavmatrix.com. Run sudo apt update by hand and fix any errors it shows, for example a third-party repository with an expired key. Run the installer again. It is safe to run it more than once.

On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W the installation takes much longer than on a Pi 4 or 5, and the installer shows a time estimate. Let it finish. Use a fast SD card and a stable power supply: an undervoltage reset during install leaves a half-finished installation.

The installer writes everything to /opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log. Terminal
sudo tail -n 100 /opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log
 Look at the last error lines. If the installer fails before it can create /opt/uavcast-pro, the log is in /tmp/uavcast-installer.log.

To list the versions available for your architecture, or to install one of them: Terminal
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | bash -s -- -l # list versions
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | <
Send /opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log, the output of cat /etc/os-release and dpkg --print-architecture, and your board model to support@uavmatrix.com. Related: Install UAVcast-Pro

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › UAVcast-Pro license won't activate
c: Copy the key from your order e-mail or your account on uavmatrix.com, and paste it into the License Key field. Typing it by hand is the most common source of errors. Make sure there are no spaces before or after the key. Press Validate.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › UAVcast-Pro license won't activate
c: Each license allows a fixed number of devices (Allowed Devices). When Remaining Devices is 0, activation fails with Maximum activations reached. Please deactivate another device first or upgrade your license. On any device where the license is active, open Application → License Manager → Activated Devices. Find the device you no longer use and press Unregister. The slot is freed straight away. Activate the new device. If you can't reach any activated device, contact support@uavmatrix.com with the license key and they can free a slot. To add slots, buy more devices for the license on uavmatrix.com.

t: Check 3: You replaced the SD card or the board
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › UAVcast-Pro license won't activate
c: The license is tied to the hardware, including the storage device. A fresh SD card, a new SSD or a new board counts as a new device and takes a new slot. Unregister the old entry in Activated Devices before or after you move, as in check 2. License already activated on this device is not an error: the key was already active here.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › UAVcast-Pro license won't activate
c: Activation contacts the UAVmatrix license server over HTTPS (port 443), so the device needs working internet at that moment. On the device, run curl -I https://uavmatrix.com. You should get an HTTP response, not a timeout. If you are on a cellular modem, check that it actually has internet: Modem connected, no internet. Check the date with date. A device with a wrong clock can't open HTTPS connections. Boards without a real-time clock set the time from the internet after boot, so wait a minute after boot and try again.

t: Check 5: Cannot connect to license service
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › UAVcast-Pro license won't activate
c:
This message means the web interface can't reach UAVcast-Pro's own background service, not the internet. Restart it and try again: Terminal
sudo systemctl restart uavcast-factory
sudo systemctl status uavcast-factory
 If it doesn't stay active (running), collect the logs with License Manager selected.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › UAVcast-Pro license won't activate
c: The license details show License Status: and Expiration Date:. An expired license must be renewed on uavmatrix.com. 64-bit operating system UAVcast-Pro v6 only runs on a 64-bit OS. If you got this far, the OS is fine; on a 32-bit OS the installer already stops with No installation candidate.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › UAVcast-Pro license won't activate
c: Download the logs with License Manager selected. They contain the response code from the license server, for example code 550 for no free slots. Send them with the first and last four characters of your key to support@uavmatrix.com. Using Fleet Manager? A license that activates fine can still be refused at pairing. See Pairing code invalid or expired. Related: Activate your license

LTE modem shows signal and an operator but the drone has no internet? Check modem type, APN, SIM PIN and data, network priority and the default route. The Modem page shows signal, an operator and maybe an IP address, yet the drone can't reach the internet: the VPN won't connect, the license can't be checked, and video and telemetry never reach the ground station over LTE. What you seeLikely causeStart at No Modem Connected Linux does not see the modem, or it lacks power Check 1 Error that mentions a HiLink modem, or no Connect button for a USB stick Wrong Modem type Check 2 Registered on the network, but no IPv4 address Wrong APN, PIN, or no data on the SIM Check 3 Modem has an IP address, internet still goes through Wi-Fi Network priority favours Wi-Fi Check 4 Works at home, not in the field (or the reverse) Roaming, coverage, or a home network on the modem subnet Check 5 <drone-ip>/modem Modem page with Traditional (PPP) selected and no modem plugged in. With a modem connected, the right-hand card shows signal quality, state, operator and IPv4 information.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › 4G modem connected but no internet
c: If the page says No Modem Connected: Check that the modem's power light is on and it sits firmly in a USB port. A modem can draw more current than a Raspberry Pi USB port supplies. Watch the dashboard's Power supply row. If it says Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply, fix the power first: Undervoltage and throttling. On the Pi, run lsusb to see the modem, and mmcli -L to see whether ModemManager found it. A HiLink modem does not show in mmcli; it appears as a network interface in ip addr instead. The modem appears on the page by itself once it is detected.

t: Check 2: Pick the right modem type
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › 4G modem connected but no internet
c: There are two kinds of USB modems, and Modem type must match yours. HiLinkTraditional (PPP) How Linux sees it A network adapter (the modem is a small router) A modem managed by ModemManager Who connects The modem itself, automatically UAVcast-Pro, with Connect and Disconnect buttons Huawei example E3372h E3372s If you choose Traditional (PPP) for a HiLink modem, the log says HiLink modem detected … Please change your modem type to 'HiLink' in settings. Change Modem type and the error goes away.

t: Check 3: APN, PIN and the SIM
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › 4G modem connected but no internet
c: For a Traditional (PPP) modem: Leave Access Point Name (Optional) empty first. UAVcast-Pro then tries your network's default APN and known APNs for the SIM, and remembers the one that works (Found a working … it will be used from now on in the log). If that fails, enter the APN your carrier gives for mobile data. Some carriers also need Username (Optional) and Password (Optional). If the SIM has a PIN, enter it in PIN code (Optional), or disable the PIN by putting the SIM in a phone. Unlock Required under Modem Information shows whether the SIM is locked. Put the SIM in a phone and check that mobile data works and the plan has data left. For a HiLink modem, the APN is set in the modem's own web page, usually at http://192.168.8.1. Open it from the Pi, or plug the modem into a laptop. UAVcast-Pro keeps trying A Traditional modem connects at boot and reconnects after signal loss by itself. If a modem connects without getting an address, UAVcast-Pro switches it to raw-IP mode and tries again. Give it a minute after boot before you change settings.

t: Check 4: Make the modem the default route
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › 4G modem connected but no internet
c:
If the Pi is also on Wi-Fi or Ethernet, traffic goes out the interface with priority, not necessarily the modem. Go to Networks. Under Network Priority, choose Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode) before flight. WiFi Priority (Indoor Mode) saves cellular data at home but sends everything over Wi-Fi. In Network Interfaces, check that the modem interface is marked Default and that Default Gateway shows via the modem interface. /networks Networks page with Auto (System Default) active and Wi-Fi (wlan0) as the default route. Select Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode) here to route over the modem. Test from the Pi over the modem alone: Terminal
ping -c 3 -I wwan0 1.1.1.1 # Traditional modem (interface name may differ)

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › 4G modem connected but no internet
c: Roaming: a SIM used abroad may need roaming enabled by the carrier. Check in a phone with the same SIM. Coverage: look at Signal Quality and Technology. Some IoT SIMs only work on certain bands or technologies. Subnet clash: HiLink modems hand out 192.168.8.x. If your home or office network also uses 192.168.8.0/24, routing breaks. Change the LAN or the modem's subnet.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › 4G modem connected but no internet
c: Download the logs with Modem Manager selected, add the output of mmcli -m 0 and ip route, and send them to support@uavmatrix.com with the modem model and carrier. Related: Cellular modem · Networks

t: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
p: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
c: UAVcast-Pro shows No heartbeat or Waiting for device? Check the USB cable, TELEM wiring, SERIAL protocol and baud rate, then use Auto-detect. The Flight Controller → Connection page shows No heartbeat, Waiting for device, Detecting baud rate or Searching, and the dashboard's Flight controller row never turns green. UAVcast-Pro can't hear the flight controller yet. The page has a live Connection check that tests each step once per second and explains the first problem it finds. Read it first: it is usually faster than this page. <drone-ip>/flight-controller The Connection check on a working link: all four steps pass. When the link fails, the first failing step is marked and explained. What you seeLikely causeStart at Waiting for device, or Flight controller plugged in: Not detected No data cable, or the board is not powered Check 1 Signal on the wire, but no readable data Wrong baud rate, TX/RX swapped, or the port is not set to MAVLink Check 2 Readable data shows a high % damaged Loose or long wire, missing ground, or electrical noise Check 3 Port shows in use by another program Something else holds the serial port Check 4 Status Off or Stopped The link is switched off Check 5
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

t: Check 1: Is the flight controller seen at all?
p: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
c: Over USB: Make sure the flight controller is powered and its USB cable goes to the companion computer. Try another cable. Many USB cables only charge and carry no data. If the board lights up but Flight controller plugged in says Not detected, the cable is the usual cause. Under Link type, choose USB and leave Port on Automatic. Automatic finds the flight controller and follows it if the device number changes. Over a TELEM port (UART / Serial): Under Link type, choose UART / Serial. Check the wiring: flight controller TX → RX on the companion computer, RX → TX, and GND → GND. A missing ground wire is a common cause. Never power the Raspberry Pi from the TELEM port. Power it separately. Raspberry Pi serial port The installer enables the Pi's UART and removes the serial console from cmdline.txt. On a Pi 3, 4 or Zero 2 W it also disables Bluetooth so the full UART is free. If you installed the OS again after UAVcast-Pro, run the installer again.

t: Check 2: Match the port settings on the flight controller
p: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
c: On a TELEM port, the flight controller must speak MAVLink at the speed UAVcast-Pro listens on. USB connections don't use a baud rate. Connect the flight controller to Mission Planner or QGroundControl over USB. Open the full parameter list and find the serial port you wired: SERIAL1 for TELEM1, SERIAL2 for TELEM2. Set SERIALx_PROTOCOL to 2 (MAVLink2). Write the parameters and reboot the flight controller. Note SERIALx_BAUD. In UAVcast-Pro, leave Baud rate on Automatic, or pick the same value. With Automatic, UAVcast-Pro tries 57600, 115200, 921600, 1500000, 460800, 230400 and 500000 baud and remembers the rate that worked. The status shows Trying … baud (n of 7) while it searches. Let UAVcast-Pro search for you Press Auto-detect. It pauses the link, listens on every port and baud rate, then saves what it finds. This can take up to a minute. If it reports No flight controller found, open Show what was tried to see each port and speed it tested.

p: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
c: If Readable flight controller data shows a percentage damaged, bytes are arriving but corrupted. This usually means a loose or long wire, a missing ground wire, or noise from motors and power cables. Re-seat the connectors and shorten the cable. Route the signal wires away from ESC and battery leads. Try a lower SERIALx_BAUD, for example 57600 or 115200.

p: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
c: The Port list marks ports that another program holds (in use by …). Stop that program, for example a MAVProxy or a second router you started yourself, or pick another port.

t: Check 5: Is the link switched on?
p: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
c: At the top of the page, Link enabled must be on. If the status says Link stopped, press Connect. Settings apply immediately, without a restart.

p: No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller
c: Download the logs with Mavlink Manager selected. The included diagnostics.txt lists the serial devices, who holds them and the USB and power events from the kernel, which is what support needs for link problems. Once the flight controller shows Connected but your ground station still waits, go to No telemetry in the ground station. Related: Flight controller connection · Hardware requirements

t: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
p: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: Flight controller connected in UAVcast-Pro but QGroundControl or Mission Planner keeps waiting? Check Enable Telemetry, the IP, UDP 14550 and VPN. UAVcast-Pro shows the flight controller as Connected, but QGroundControl says Waiting for vehicle connection or Mission Planner times out with No heartbeat packets received. The drone hears the flight controller; the telemetry just doesn't reach your ground station. If UAVcast-Pro itself shows No heartbeat, fix that first: No MAVLink heartbeat. What you seeLikely causeStart at Dashboard: Ground station None set up, or Not sending No destination, or Enable Telemetry is off Check 1 Dashboard says Sending, the GCS sees nothing Wrong IP, firewall, or the GCS listens on another port Check 2 Worked on Wi-Fi, nothing over 4G Destination is a local IP instead of the VPN IP Check 3 Used to connect over TCP 5760, stopped after an update TCP 5760 was closed in v6.5.0 Check 4 Telemetry shows, but commands and mode changes do nothing Read Only is on for this destination Check 5
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

p: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: Open Dashboard and read the Ground station row in the status card. None set up: there is no destination. Add one in step 2. Not sending: a destination exists but nothing goes out. Sending to … · n packets/s: telemetry leaves the drone. Go to check 2. Go to Ground Control Stations. Press Add Destination if the list is empty. On the card for your computer, switch on Enable Endpoint and Enable Telemetry. Both video and telemetry are off on a new destination. Enter the computer's IPv4 address in Destination IP or Host and keep Telemetry Port at 14550. <drone-ip>/ground-control Ground Control Stations: a destination with Enable Telemetry on. Invalid addresses are skipped UAVcast-Pro only accepts IPv4 addresses such as 192.168.1.10. If you try to save a hostname, you get Enter a valid IPv4 address, for example 192.168.1.10. An address that is missing or invalid is left out of the telemetry router, and the Connection check on the Flight Controller page lists it.

t: Check 2: Make sure the ground station listens
p: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: UAVcast-Pro sends MAVLink over UDP to the address and port you set. The ground station must listen on that port. QGroundControl listens on UDP 14550 by default. If you changed Telemetry Port, add a UDP comm link on the same port in Application Settings → Comm Links. Mission Planner: choose UDP in the connection drop-down at the top right, press Connect and accept port 14550. Only one program can listen on a port. Close MAVProxy, a second QGroundControl or another tool that may hold 14550. Allow incoming UDP 14550 in the firewall. The commands are in No video, check 3.

t: Check 3: Use the VPN address over cellular
p: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: Over 4G the drone can't reach a local address like 192.168.1.20. Put your computer's VPN address (Fleet Manager VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier) in Destination IP or Host. From the computer, ping the drone's VPN address. If the ping fails, the VPN is the problem: see VPN connected but can't reach the drone.

p: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: Since v6.5.0 the telemetry router does not accept TCP connections on port 5760, so only the ground stations you add, and switch on, get data. If you used to connect Mission Planner over TCP 5760, add your computer as a destination and connect over UDP instead.

p: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: If telemetry shows but arming, mode changes or mission uploads do nothing, check Read Only on that destination. Read Only blocks everything that would change the vehicle (commands, mode changes, parameter and mission writes), so the ground station can only watch. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes. Some ground stations show warnings in this mode because some of their requests go unanswered.

p: No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: Download the logs with Mavlink Manager selected and send them to support@uavmatrix.com. Mention which ground station you use and its IP address. Related: Ground Control Stations · Ports and protocols

t: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
p: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: Telemetry works but video stays black in QGroundControl or Mission Planner? Check the camera, Enable Video, the destination IP, UDP 5600 and the GCS. Telemetry arrives and the drone shows on the map, but the video area stays black, or QGroundControl's video window says WAITING FOR VIDEO. Work through the checks in order. Most cases are solved by check 2 or 3. QGroundControl The symptom in QGroundControl: telemetry arrives (Not Ready, Stabilize in the toolbar; No GPS Lock because this bench setup has no GPS), but the video window in the bottom-left corner says WAITING FOR VIDEO. What you seeLikely causeStart at Video is black in the GCS and in the UAVcast-Pro live preview The camera is not running on the drone Check 1 Live preview works, the ground station stays black Enable Video is off for this ground station, or the IP is wrong Check 2 Worked on Wi-Fi at home, black over 4G The destination uses a local IP instead of the VPN IP Check 2 Everything looks right, still black on Windows The firewall blocks incoming UDP on port 5600 Check 3 QGroundControl shows video, Mission Planner does not Mission Planner has no GStreamer source set Check 4
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

t: Check 1: Confirm the camera is streaming on the drone
p: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: If the drone isn't producing video, no ground station setting will help. Open the UAVcast-Pro web interface and go to Camera → Camera settings. Check that Enable Camera? is Yes and that a camera is chosen in Select Camera. Check that the camera runs: the dashboard's Video row should say Running. If it is stopped, press Start on the Camera page (the button reads Restart while the camera runs). Turn on Enable Live Preview? and look at Live Preview. If you see a picture, the camera works and you can go to check 2. If Select Camera says No cameras available, go to Camera not detected. <drone-ip>/camera Camera → Camera settings with CAM 1 enabled. Live Preview shows No Video Available until Enable Live Preview? is ticked. The preview is not the ground station stream The browser preview goes through the built-in media server (WebRTC on port 8889). The ground station gets a separate H.264 stream over UDP. A working preview proves the camera works, not that the UDP stream reaches your laptop. If the Action Logs on the Camera page say a camera does not support a resolution, pick another value in Resolution. UAVcast-Pro falls back to the largest supported size and logs which one it used.

t: Check 2: Check the ground station destination
p: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: UAVcast-Pro only sends video to destinations where video is switched on. Telemetry and video have separate switches, and both are off on a new destination. Go to Ground Control Stations and find the card for the computer that runs your ground station. Make sure Enable Endpoint and Enable Video are both on. Check Destination IP or Host. It must be the IPv4 address of the ground station computer as seen from the drone. Hostnames are not accepted. Check that Video Port is 5600, or the port your ground station listens on. Fields save when you leave them or press Enter. A green tick confirms the save. <drone-ip>/ground-control Ground Control Stations: a destination with Enable Video on and Video Port 5600. Flying over 4G? Use the VPN IP Over a cellular link the drone can't reach your laptop's local address (like 192.168.1.20). Use the address your laptop has on the VPN (Fleet Manager VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier). On Windows, run ipconfig and look for the Tailscale or ZeroTier adapter. Using Fleet Manager? Destinations are created for you when you add a stream binding, and each extra drone on the same ground station gets its own ports. Check the video port shown on the binding, not 5600. See Stream bindings.

t: Check 3: Allow UDP 5600 through the firewall
p: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c:
Video arrives as incoming UDP traffic. On Windows this is blocked by default, even when telemetry gets through because the ground station asked for an exception. Windows Linux macOS Open PowerShell as Administrator and run: PowerShell (Administrator)PowerShell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "UAV Video" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 5600 -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -

t: Check 4: Set up video in your ground station
p: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c:
QGroundControl Mission Planner Click the Q icon, then Application Settings. Open the video settings (Video, or General → Video in older versions). Set Source to UDP h.264 Video Stream, and check that the UDP address uses port 5600 (UDP URL 0.0.0.0:5600 in current versions, UDP Port 5600 in older ones). Go back to the Fly view. The video tile should show a picture within a few seconds. Mission Planner shows video in the HUD. If it stays black, set the source by hand: Right-click the HUD and choose Video → Set GStreamer Source. Paste this pipeline and confirm: Mission Planner GStreamer sourceText
udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=video, clock-rate=90000, encoding-name=H264, payload=96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=BGRA ! appsink name=outsink

t: Check 5: Test the stream without a ground station
p: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c:
This takes the ground station software out of the picture. If a window with video opens, the drone, network and firewall are fine and the problem is in the GCS settings. Windows, Linux and macOSTerminal
gst-launch-1.0 -v udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)video, clock-rate=(int)90000, encoding-name=(string)H264" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264

p: No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner
c: Download the logs with Camera Server selected in the log list, and send them to support@uavmatrix.com together with your UAVcast-Pro version, the camera model and the ground station you use. Related: Camera settings · Ground Control Stations

Fix Invalid pairing code, This pairing code has expired and License is not owned by any member of this organization when pairing a UAV with Fleet Manager. You entered the code from UAVcast-Pro in Fleet Manager's Pair Device wizard, and it was refused. Pairing works in this direction: UAVcast-Pro shows the code, you type it into Fleet Manager. The code has 8 digits and is valid for 5 minutes. fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/pair-device Fleet Manager refusing a code: the error appears as a toast on the Pairing Code step, here This pairing code has expired. k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Pairing code invalid or expired
c: In UAVcast-Pro, go to Fleet Management and press Connect to Fleet Manager. Copy the 8 digits shown under Pairing Code. In Fleet Manager, go to Fleet → Pair Device, choose the organization and enter the code under Enter Pairing Code.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Pairing code invalid or expired
c: A code is valid for 5 minutes and works once. When Expires in reaches zero, press Connect to Fleet Manager again in UAVcast-Pro for a new code. If UAVcast-Pro can't get a code at all, it shows Unable to connect to Fleet Manager. Please check your internet connection.: fix the drone's internet first.

t: Check 3: License owned by someone outside the organization
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Pairing code invalid or expired
c: Fleet Manager only accepts a drone whose UAVcast-Pro license was bought by a member of the organization you pair into. The match is made on the e-mail address of the store account that owns the license. Fix it one of these ways: Invite the account that bought the license to the organization (Team), then pair again. Pair into an organization where the license owner is a member. If the license was bought with another e-mail address of yours, ask support@uavmatrix.com to add that address as a license e-mail on your Fleet Manager user. See Licenses in Fleet Manager.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Pairing code invalid or expired
c: Open Application → License Manager on the drone and check License Status. An expired or refunded license must be renewed on uavmatrix.com. If UAVcast-Pro itself has no active license, it can't request a code (No valid license found. Please activate your license first.): see License won't activate.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Pairing code invalid or expired
c: A UAV belongs to one organization. To move it, remove it from the old organization first. Re-pairing into the same organization is allowed and keeps the UAV's history. See Remove or transfer a UAV.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › Pairing code invalid or expired
c: Send the exact error text, the UAV hostname and the organization name to support@uavmatrix.com. Related: Fleet Manager pairing in UAVcast-Pro · Pair your first UAV

NTRIP stuck on Connecting, no RTCM forwarded or no RTK Fixed? Check caster host, port, mountpoint, credentials, GGA upstream and the GPS receiver. Under Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK the status does not reach Streaming corrections, RTCM messages forwarded stays at zero, or corrections flow but the flight controller never gets past 3D fix or RTK Float. The chain has four links: internet → caster → UAVcast-Pro → flight controller → GPS receiver. Find the first one that breaks. <drone-ip>/flight-controller Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK on a unit without a caster configured: status Disabled, counters at zero and Caster response empty. Healthy is Streaming corrections, a 200 caster response and climbing counters. What you seeLikely causeStart at Status Connecting or Error, no caster response Wrong host or port, TLS mismatch, or no internet Check 1 Caster response 401 Unauthorized Wrong username, password or mountpoint Check 2 Log says caster returned sourcetable The mountpoint name is wrong Check 2 Connected, but no RTCM data, reconnects every few seconds The caster needs a GGA position first Check 3 RTCM forwarded, fix stays at 3D fix Flight controller link down, or receiver not RTK-capable Check 4 RTK Float, never RTK Fixed Sky view, distance to the base, or time Check 5
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › RTK corrections not arriving
c: Check Caster host and Port. Most public casters use plain TCP on port 2101. Use TLS (HTTPS) must match the caster. Commercial casters (Trimble, Hexagon, Topcon and others) often need TLS, usually still on port 2101, sometimes 2102 or 443. Public casters normally don't use TLS. Make sure the drone has internet. Dashboard → Cellular should be connected. If not, see Modem connected, no internet. Some cellular plans block unusual outbound ports. If the caster offers port 443, try it.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › RTK corrections not arriving
c: Press Test connection. Caster accepted the credentials. means username and password are right. For rtk2go.com, use a real e-mail address as Username and leave Password empty. Press Browse mountpoints and pick a mountpoint from the list instead of typing the name. Prefer one close to where you fly. If the caster answers with its sourcetable instead of data, the NTRIP log says caster returned sourcetable — check mountpoint. The mountpoint name is wrong or no longer exists.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › RTK corrections not arriving
c: VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters only send corrections after they know where you are. The NMEA column in the mountpoint browser says Required for those mountpoints. Turn on Send GGA upstream (on by default). Send interval (seconds) defaults to 10. Position source: Live position from flight controller is right in flight. Until the flight controller reports a GPS fix, UAVcast-Pro uses the Fixed manual position, so enter a latitude and longitude near you for bench tests. Watch Last GGA sent update. UAVcast-Pro reconnects by itself when the caster goes quiet, and the log shows no data from caster for …s — reconnecting. After a short internet drop, corrections resume within seconds.

t: Check 4: From UAVcast-Pro to the receiver
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › RTK corrections not arriving
c: Corrections reach the GPS through the flight controller link, as MAVLink GPS_RTCM_DATA. The flight controller must be Connected on Flight Controller → Connection. If not, see No MAVLink heartbeat. Look at the GPS quality card. No RTK status from receiver means the flight controller has never reported RTK status. The connected GPS is usually not RTK-capable: RTK needs a carrier-phase RTK receiver such as a u-blox F9P, Here3+ or Septentrio Mosaic. A standard M8N or M10 navigation module won't do RTK. Recent message types should include the constellations your receiver uses (for example 1077 GPS, 1087 GLONASS, 1097 Galileo, 1127 BeiDou) and a base position message (1005 or 1006).

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › RTK corrections not arriving
c: Give the antenna open sky. Trees, buildings and the drone's own electronics cause multipath and noise. Wait. A cold start can take a minute or two even in good conditions. Pick a closer base. Accuracy and the chance of a fix drop with distance from the base station. Last correction in GPS quality should stay at a few seconds. If it grows, corrections are being lost on the link.

b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › RTK corrections not arriving
c: Download the logs with NTRIP Client selected and send them, with your caster provider and GPS model, to support@uavmatrix.com. The full setup is in Set up RTK with an NTRIP caster. Related: NTRIP / RTK settings

UAVcast-Pro warns Voltage too low or Slowed down? Size the power supply for Pi, modem and camera, fix thin cables and cooling, and stop resets. The dashboard's Power supply row shows a warning, the modem drops, the flight controller link resets, or the Pi reboots in flight. On a drone, an undersized power supply causes more strange faults than any software setting. <drone-ip>/ Dashboard → status card. The Power supply row is under System; here it reads Stable. Warnings replace that text, as listed below. Power supply rowMeaning Stable No undervoltage or throttling since boot Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply The supply voltage is below what the Pi needs right now Voltage dropped since start-up It happened earlier, for example when the modem connected or the motors spun up Slowed down (heat or power) The CPU is running slower to protect itself from heat or low voltage The readings come from the Raspberry Pi firmware, so they are only available on a Raspberry Pi.
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

t: Check 1: Size the supply for everything on it
c: The Pi powers the modem and USB camera through its USB ports. A 4G modem draws its peak current when it connects and when the signal is weak. Use a 5 V BEC or regulator rated well above the total current of the Pi, modem, camera and anything else on the same rail. The official Raspberry Pi power supply specs list what each model needs. Never power the Pi from the flight controller's TELEM or USB port. If the modem draws more than the Pi can pass through, power the modem from the regulator directly, through a powered USB hub or a USB cable with separate power.
Thin or long cables lose voltage under load. Use short, thick power leads and a good USB cable for the modem. A cable that is fine for a phone charger can still cause undervoltage at peak current.

Temperature under System Information shows the CPU temperature. A Pi that runs video encoding inside a closed airframe in the sun gets hot. Add a heat sink or a small fan, and give the enclosure airflow. A Pi 5 needs active cooling for continuous encoding.
Voltage dropped since start-up stays until the next boot. Reboot, run a typical mission on the bench (modem connected, camera streaming), and confirm the row stays Stable.

The log download includes power and USB events from the kernel in diagnostics.txt. Download the logs and send them to support@uavmatrix.com with a photo of your power wiring. Related: Hardware requirements · Dashboard

t: Check 1: Authorize the drone on the network
p: VPN connected but can't reach the drone
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › VPN connected but can't reach the drone
c: ZeroTier: In UAVcast-Pro, open Virtual Private Network. Check that Enable VPN is Yes, Services is ZeroTier, and the Network ID is the one from your ZeroTier controller. Look at your network under Connected Networks. If its status badge says ACCESS_DENIED, the drone joined but is not authorized. In your ZeroTier controller, open the network and authorize the member with the drone's node ID. Back in UAVcast-Pro, wait until the network shows status OK and an IP address. That is the address you use from the laptop. On a private ZeroTier network, every device that joins (drone, laptop, tablet) must be authorized once in the controller before it gets an address. (UAVnet networks are private too; UAVnet is being retired, so move to the Fleet Manager VPN.) Tailscale: the drone shows Connected with an IPv4 Address (100.x.y.z) when it is in. If it says Not Connected, use Web Login → Generate Login URL, or the Auth Key tab with a key from your Tailscale admin console.

t: Check 2: Put the laptop on the same network
p: VPN connected but can't reach the drone
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › VPN connected but can't reach the drone
c: Both ends must be on the same ZeroTier network or the same tailnet. ZeroTier: on the laptop, join the same Network ID and authorize the laptop in your controller too. On Windows, check the ZeroTier tray icon; on Linux run sudo zerotier-cli listnetworks. The status must be OK. Tailscale: a Tailscale client is on one tailnet at a time. On the laptop, run tailscale status. The drone must be in the list. If not, the laptop is logged in to another account or tailnet. Fleet Manager VPN: if the drone was paired with Fleet Manager and VPN, it is on your organization's network, not your personal Tailscale. Connect the laptop with the command Fleet Manager gives under Network (tailscale up --login-server=… --authkey=…) and run it on the laptop, never on the drone. See Connect a ground station. Pairing can replace the drone's VPN When you pair a drone in Fleet Manager with Replace existing VPN with Fleet Manager network, the drone leaves its current Tailscale network and joins the organization's network. Laptops on the old tailnet can no longer reach it.

p: VPN connected but can't reach the drone
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › VPN connected but can't reach the drone
c: Tailscale device keys expire. When the drone's key expires it drops off the tailnet until it logs in again. The Expires field on the Virtual Private Network page shows the date. In the Tailscale admin console you can turn off key expiry for the drone, so it doesn't drop off in the middle of a project.

t: Check 4: The drone needs internet first
p: VPN connected but can't reach the drone
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › VPN connected but can't reach the drone
c: The VPN runs over the drone's own internet connection. If the modem has no internet, the VPN shows as disconnected or never gets an address. Fix the connection first: Modem connected, no internet.

p: VPN connected but can't reach the drone
b: Troubleshooting & FAQ › VPN connected but can't reach the drone
c: If ping <drone-vpn-ip> works: Web interface: open http://<drone-vpn-ip>/. The live preview also needs port 8889 to be reachable over the VPN. Telemetry and video: these are sent from the drone to the address in Ground Control Stations → Destination IP or Host. It must be the laptop's VPN address, not the drone's, and not the laptop's Wi-Fi address. Then see No telemetry or No video. Slow, but working: Tailscale shows the Relay in use. A relayed connection works but adds delay. Some cellular networks don't allow direct connections, so a relay may be the best you get on that carrier.

On the device, run: Terminal
sudo systemctl status uavcast-web

sudo systemctl restart uavcast-web
journalctl -u uavcast-web --since "1 hour ago"

Set up a Raspberry Pi camera or USB webcam in UAVcast-Pro and stream low-latency H.264 video over UDP to QGroundControl or Mission Planner. Resolution, FPS and bitrate. UAVcast-Pro captures video from a Raspberry Pi CSI camera or a USB webcam, encodes it as H.264 and sends it as RTP over UDP to every ground station that has Enable Video turned on. Mission Planner and QGroundControl play it directly on port 5600. A copy of the stream feeds the live preview in the web interface and the on-drone recorder. Open Camera → Camera settings. <drone-ip>/camera Camera → Camera settings with a Raspberry Pi camera as CAM 1 at 1536×864 and 30 FPS, bitrate Auto. Live Preview is off here.
k: UAVcast-Pro, UAVmatrix, Fleet Manager, drone 4G LTE, MAVLink, ArduPilot, PX4, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, Raspberry Pi drone video

c: Connect the camera and go to Camera → Camera settings. Set Enable Camera? to Yes. Click the CAM 1 slot and pick the camera. CSI cameras show as Raspberry Pi Camera - imx708 (CSI) or similar; USB cameras by their name. Under Camera Settings, pick a Resolution your camera supports. Unsupported sizes are marked. Leave Select FPS on Auto and Bitrate at 0 (auto) to start with. Under Stream Settings, tick Enable Live Preview? and select Start. On Ground Control Stations, turn on Enable Video for each ground station that should get video. If no camera appears in the list, see the Action Logs at the bottom of the page: they show every device the camera detector checked and why it was skipped.

CAM 1 Raspberry Pi camera Detected cameras, Enter Custom Pipeline Pick Enter Custom Pipeline to write your own GStreamer pipeline. See Custom pipeline. Resolution 640x480 Sizes the camera reports If the camera can't deliver the size, UAVcast-Pro falls back to the largest supported size and logs which one it used. Select FPS Auto Auto or the rates the camera supports at this resolution Auto lets the camera choose. Bitrate 0 (Auto) 0–10000 kbps, in steps of 100 Set a fixed value for cellular links. Stream Recovery Rate Auto Auto (0), 1, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120 frames Keyframe interval. Lower values recover faster after packet loss and fix grey smearing over VPN, at the cost of bandwidth. Flip Settings Off Vertical Flip, Horizontal Flip CSI cameras. Rotation 0° 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° USB and other non-CSI cameras. Enable Live Preview? On On, off Preview on this page and on the Flight Map. Recording also uses this copy of the stream. Settings save as you change them. If a running stream doesn't pick up a change, select Restart under Stream Settings.

There's no single right setting: the bitrate must fit inside the slowest part of the link with room left for telemetry. Starting points for one camera: LinkResolutionFPSBitrateStream Recovery Rate Local Wi-Fi or Ethernet 1920x1080 30 4000–6000 kbps Auto Good 4G/LTE 1280x720 30 1500–2500 kbps 30 frames Weak 4G or long range 1280x720 or 854x480 15–20 800–1200 kbps 15 frames If the picture freezes or smears grey after packet loss, lower the bitrate first, then lower Stream Recovery Rate so keyframes come more often.

The System load indicator shows how hard the encoder works. On a Raspberry Pi 5 every stream is encoded in software (the Pi 5 has no H.264 encoder), so high resolutions or two streams can max out the CPU. When it warns CPU is near its limit. Lower the resolution or bitrate., do that before you fly.

Live Preview plays the stream in the browser through the built-in media server (WebRTC on port 8889). It's a few hundred milliseconds behind the UDP stream your ground station gets, depending on the network. Use the open-in-new-tab button to watch it full screen. Browsers start the preview muted; unmute it in the player if you use audio. The preview needs the browser to reach port 8889 on the drone directly. It works on the LAN and over a VPN, but not through Fleet Manager's Open via Proxy, which only carries the web interface. Use Open via VPN for the preview.

Add sound from a USB microphone or a webcam's built-in mic to the UAVcast-Pro live preview, and send it to ground stations as an RTP/Opus stream on Video Port + 2. UAVcast-Pro can add sound from a USB microphone or a USB camera's built-in mic. Audio is encoded as Opus, which costs little CPU and bandwidth. It always plays in the live preview, and you can also send it to your ground stations as a separate RTP stream. Find it in the Audio card on Camera → Camera settings.

c: Plug in a USB microphone, or use a webcam with a built-in mic. On Camera → Camera settings, turn on Audio. Leave Audio device on Auto (camera microphone if present), or pick a device. Use Test tone (no microphone needed) to test the path without a mic. Watch the indicator. Audio live with a moving level meter means sound is captured. In Live Preview, unmute the player. Browsers start the preview muted. <drone-ip>/camera Camera → Audio, switched off. Turn it on to choose the microphone and bitrate. A microphone that fails never interrupts the video. The indicator shows Audio error with the reason instead.

Turn on Send audio to ground stations. UAVcast-Pro then sends a separate RTP/Opus stream to every ground station that receives video, on that destination's Video Port + 2. With the default video port that's 5602. Two destinations on the same computer therefore need video ports at least 3 apart, for example 5600 and 5603. QGroundControl and Mission Planner ignore audio. Play it with GStreamer: On the ground stationTerminal
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5602 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)audio, clock-rate=(int)48000, encoding-name=(string)OPUS, payload=(int)97" ! rtpopusdepay ! opusdec

When the built-in camera support doesn't cover your camera, give UAVcast-Pro your own GStreamer pipeline. Typical cases are an RTSP IP or gimbal camera, a thermal camera, H.265, or sending to a fixed address. c: Go to Camera → Camera settings. Click the CAM 1 slot and choose Enter Custom Pipeline. Type the pipeline in Custom Pipeline, without the gst-launch-1.0 prefix. (If you paste it with the prefix, UAVcast-Pro strips it.) Select Start (or Restart) and check the Action Logs for errors. Video Port and Enable Video on Ground Control Stations have no effect: put the ground station's address and port in the pipeline's udpsink. b: UAVcast-Pro › Camera & video › Custom GStreamer pipeline
c: With Enable Live Preview? ticked, UAVcast-Pro adds a branch to your pipeline that sends the encoded video to the built-in media server, so the preview, the Flight Map video window and recording keep working. It finds the right place automatically: If your pipeline has tee name=t, it adds a branch from that tee. Otherwise it splits the stream just before rtph264pay or rtph265pay. For an RTSP source without a recognised parser, it leaves the pipeline as it is, and there's no preview. For the most predictable result, end your encoded stream with h264parse and a tee name=t, and put your own udpsink on a branch of that tee.

b: UAVcast-Pro › Camera & video › Custom GStreamer pipeline
c: Dual stream, RC switching and per-camera settings don't apply to a custom pipeline. The pipeline is the whole video setup. Resolution, FPS, bitrate and flip settings are hidden, because the pipeline sets them.

t: Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
p: Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
c: Connect two cameras to UAVcast-Pro and switch between them from your RC transmitter, or stream both at once to QGroundControl or Mission Planner on separate UDP ports. UAVcast-Pro handles two cameras, for example a forward FPV camera and a downward or gimbal camera. You can use them in two ways: Switching: one stream, and you choose which camera feeds it, from the web interface or from an RC channel on your transmitter. Uses the bandwidth and CPU of one stream. Dual stream: both cameras stream at the same time, each to its own UDP port, each with its own resolution, FPS and bitrate. Uses twice the bandwidth and CPU. Supported combinations: CSI + USB, two USB cameras, or two CSI cameras on boards with two camera connectors (Raspberry Pi 5, Compute Module carrier boards).

p: Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream

c: Go to Camera → Camera settings. Make sure CAM 1 has a camera. Select Add Camera next to CAM 1 and pick the second camera. It appears in the CAM 2 slot. Click a slot to make that camera the active one (Click to switch to Camera 2). In switching mode both cameras share Camera 1's resolution and frame rate (Resolution and FPS from Camera 1 will be used). If Camera 2 doesn't support that size, it uses its native resolution and is scaled, unless you turn on Match Camera 1 Resolution for a camera that supports it.

p: Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
b: UAVcast-Pro › Camera & video › Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
c: RC Channel Switching appears when two cameras are set and dual stream is off. On your transmitter, assign a two-position switch to a free channel, for example channel 7. Check in Mission Planner or on Flight Map → Radio that the channel moves between about 1000 and 2000 µs. Under RC Channel Switching, turn on Enable RC channel camera switching. Pick the RC Channel. Flip the switch and watch Current PWM. Below 1500 selects Camera 1, above 1500 selects Camera 2. <drone-ip>/camera The camera slots: CAM 1 in use and Add Camera for the second camera. RC Channel Switching shows up once both slots are filled and dual stream is off. While RC switching is on, clicking a camera slot does nothing: the transmitter is in control. Turn RC switching off to choose cameras by hand. SettingDefaultValuesNotes Enable RC channel camera switching Off On, off RC Channel Channel 7 Channel 1–18 Read from the flight controller's RC input. Switch point 1500 µs fixed PWM < 1500 = Camera 1, PWM > 1500 = Camera 2.

t: Stream both cameras at once (dual stream)
p: Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
b: UAVcast-Pro › Camera & video › Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
c:
With two cameras set, turn on Dual stream on the Camera page. The badge shows Both live. Under Per-camera settings, set resolution, FPS and bitrate for each camera. On Ground Control Stations, each destination now has Video Port (Camera 2). Leave it empty to use Video Port + 1 (5601), or enter another port. With several destinations on one computer, space their video ports 3 apart (5600, 5603 …) so camera 2 and audio don't land on another destination's port. Set up a second video receiver on the ground station for that port. Camera 1 goes to each ground station's Video Port (default 5600), Camera 2 to Video Port (Camera 2) (default 5601). QGroundControl shows one video stream at a time. To watch Camera 2, run a second receiver, for example a second QGroundControl instance on port 5601, Mission Planner with a GStreamer source on 5601, or GStreamer directly: Terminal
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5601 caps=<

p: Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
b: UAVcast-Pro › Camera & video › Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream
c: Second camera missing from the list: two CSI cameras need a board with two camera ports. On a Raspberry Pi, reboot after installing UAVcast-Pro: the installer enlarges the camera memory pool (CMA) so two cameras can run together. Camera 2 picture stretched: Camera 2 is scaled to Camera 1's resolution in switching mode. Use cameras with the same aspect ratio, or turn on Match Camera 1 Resolution. Switch does nothing: check Current PWM. No signal means the flight controller isn't reporting RC input on that channel.

Record camera video and MAVLink telemetry on the drone with UAVcast-Pro, automatically when armed, to the SD card or a USB SSD, and review flights with video, map and data. UAVcast-Pro records each flight on the drone itself: the camera video and a MAVLink telemetry log (.tlog). Recording uses the stream that is already encoded, so it costs no extra CPU and never interrupts the live video to your ground station. Because the files are written on the drone, you get full-quality video even when the cellular link drops. Recordings start automatically when you arm, or by hand from the Flight Map. Requires v6.5.1 or later. Open Camera → Recordings. It has two tabs: Library and Settings. <drone-ip>/camera Camera → Recordings → Library with two recorded flights.
